Two days before Marine Day in July |rituals = [[Chakkirako]] (UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage) }} '''Kainan Shrine''' (海南神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Miura, Kanagawa|ja|三浦市}}, {{ill|Kanagawa Prefecture|ja|神奈川県}}, slightly inland from {{ill|Misaki Fishing Port|ja|三崎漁港}}. It is the total guardian shrine of the {{ill|Miura Peninsula|ja|三浦半島}} in {{ill|Sagami Province|ja|相模国}}, enshrining Fujiwara Sukemitsu, Mitsuwatari-hime, Senryū Benzaiten (part of the Miura Shichifukujin), and Jinushi-no-Ōkami. The shrine has a deep connection to {{ill|Minamoto no Yoritomo|ja|源頼朝}}, who revered it, and it features sacred trees planted by Yoritomo, including a dragon-shaped sacred ginkgo tree. [[Kainan Shrine]] is a regional [[Sōja (Shinto)|Sōja shrine]]. It enshrines many kami of the local region. It contrasts with provincial Soja shrines which enshrine all the kami of a provincehttps://archive.ph/wip/XtZfZ == Enshrined Deities == * '''Fujiwara Sukemitsu (藤原資盈)''' * '''Mitsuwatari-hime (盈渡姫)''' * '''Jinushi-no-Ōkami (地主大神)''' * '''Susanoo (素戔嗚尊)''' * '''{{ill|Otori-sama|ja|天日鷲神}} (天日鷲神)''' * '''Sugawara no Michizane (菅原道真)''' * '''Senryū Benzaiten (筌龍弁財天)''' == History == During the reign of {{ill|Emperor Seiwa|ja|清和天皇}}, Fujiwara Sukemitsu was exiled due to a false accusation related to a succession dispute. In {{ill|Jōgan (era)|ja|貞観}} 6 (864 CE), Sukemitsu was shipwrecked on the {{ill|Miura Peninsula|ja|三浦半島}} while traveling to his post in {{ill|Tsukushi Province|ja|筑紫国}}. The locals revered Sukemitsu for his efforts in quelling pirates and improving welfare. After his death in Jōgan 8 (866 CE), a shrine was built to honor him. In {{ill|Tengen (era)|ja|天元}} 5 (982 CE), the current shrine building was established, and the shrine became the total guardian of {{ill|Miura District, Kanagawa|ja|三浦郡}}. Minamoto no Yoritomo, following his 1180 uprising, held the shrine in high regard. Legend states that Yoritomo planted a pair of sacred ginkgo trees as offerings in 1185. The shrine received the title of "Sōchinju" (総鎮守, General Guardian Shrine) of the Miura Peninsula in 1719 (Kyōhō 4). It was designated a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}} in 1873 (Meiji 6) and listed as a shrine for offering government-provided ritual offerings in 1907 (Meiji 40). The ritual {{ill|Chakkirako|ja|チャッキラコ}}, unique to the shrine, was inscribed as a UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage in 2009. The shrine's buildings were designated as Important Cultural Properties by Kanagawa Prefecture in 2011. In 2021, the shrine became the guardian of the "Animal Shichifukujin" statues from the defunct Keikyu Aburatsubo Marine Park. == Shrine Grounds == === Main Features === * '''Main Hall (本殿)''' - Built in [[Shimmei-zukuri]] style. * '''Worship Hall (拝殿)''' - [[Gongen-zukuri]] style. * '''Sacred Ginkgo Trees''' - Planted by Minamoto no Yoritomo, the female tree's drooping branches symbolize fertility and are touched by women seeking blessings for lactation and childbirth. The male tree resembles a dragon. Designated as a Natural Monument of Miura City. === Sub-Shrines === * '''Ryūjin and Suijin Shrines''' - Sacred to water and dragon deities. * '''Hōsō Shrine''' - Dedicated to Minamoto no Tametomo, protector against disease. * '''Kōya Shrine''' - Worships Iwaka Mutsukari no Mikoto, the deity of cuisine and cooking. * '''Mitama Shrine''' - Dedicated to Kamakura Goro Kagemasa, believed to heal eye diseases. * '''Fukutoku Inari Shrine''' - For prosperity and safety in trade and fishing. * '''Konpira Shrine''' - Dedicated to Ōmononushi, a deity of maritime safety and commerce. === Notable Festivals and Rituals === * '''New Year's Eve (January 1)''' - Saitan-sai with lion dances for exorcism. * '''January 15''' - {{ill|Chakkirako}}: A unique dance registered as a UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage. * '''Summer Festival''' - Two-day event with traditional mikoshi processions. * '''Menkagura (November)''' - A traditional masked dance representing local folklore and Shinto traditions. == Access == * From '''Keikyu Kurihama Line''': - Take a bus from Miura-Kaigan Station or Misaki-guchi Station to Misaki Port (三崎港), then walk 2 minutes north. * Parking available near the shrine office. == References == {{reflist}} == See Also == * {{ill|Power spots|ja|パワースポット}} * {{ill|Minamoto no Yoritomo|ja|源頼朝}} * {{ill|Ryūjin|ja|龍神}} [[Category:Shrines in Kanagawa Prefecture]] Two days before Marine Day in July |rituals = [[Chakkirako]] (UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage) }} '''Kainan Shrine''' (海南神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Miura, Kanagawa|ja|三浦市}}, {{ill|Kanagawa Prefecture|ja|神奈川県}}, slightly inland from {{ill|Misaki Fishing Port|ja|三崎漁港}}. It is the total guardian shrine of the {{ill|Miura Peninsula|ja|三浦半島}} in {{ill|Sagami Province|ja|相模国}}, enshrining Fujiwara Sukemitsu, Mitsuwatari-hime, Senryū Benzaiten (part of the Miura Shichifukujin), and Jinushi-no-Ōkami. The shrine has a deep connection to {{ill|Minamoto no Yoritomo|ja|源頼朝}}, who revered it, and it features sacred trees planted by Yoritomo, including a dragon-shaped sacred ginkgo tree. [[Kainan Shrine]] is a regional [[Sōja (Shinto)|Sōja shrine]]. It enshrines many kami of the local region. It contrasts with provincial Soja shrines which enshrine all the kami of a provincehttps://archive.ph/wip/XtZfZ == Enshrined Deities == * '''Fujiwara Sukemitsu (藤原資盈)''' * '''Mitsuwatari-hime (盈渡姫)''' * '''Jinushi-no-Ōkami (地主大神)''' * '''Susanoo (素戔嗚尊)''' * '''{{ill|Otori-sama|ja|天日鷲神}} (天日鷲神)''' * '''Sugawara no Michizane (菅原道真)''' * '''Senryū Benzaiten (筌龍弁財天)''' == History == During the reign of {{ill|Emperor Seiwa|ja|清和天皇}}, Fujiwara Sukemitsu was exiled due to a false accusation related to a succession dispute. In {{ill|Jōgan (era)|ja|貞観}} 6 (864 CE), Sukemitsu was shipwrecked on the {{ill|Miura Peninsula|ja|三浦半島}} while traveling to his post in {{ill|Tsukushi Province|ja|筑紫国}}. The locals revered Sukemitsu for his efforts in quelling pirates and improving welfare. After his death in Jōgan 8 (866 CE), a shrine was built to honor him. In {{ill|Tengen (era)|ja|天元}} 5 (982 CE), the current shrine building was established, and the shrine became the total guardian of {{ill|Miura District, Kanagawa|ja|三浦郡}}. Minamoto no Yoritomo, following his 1180 uprising, held the shrine in high regard. Legend states that Yoritomo planted a pair of sacred ginkgo trees as offerings in 1185. The shrine received the title of "Sōchinju" (総鎮守, General Guardian Shrine) of the Miura Peninsula in 1719 (Kyōhō 4). It was designated a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}} in 1873 (Meiji 6) and listed as a shrine for offering government-provided ritual offerings in 1907 (Meiji 40). The ritual {{ill|Chakkirako|ja|チャッキラコ}}, unique to the shrine, was inscribed as a UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage in 2009. The shrine's buildings were designated as Important Cultural Properties by Kanagawa Prefecture in 2011. In 2021, the shrine became the guardian of the "Animal Shichifukujin" statues from the defunct Keikyu Aburatsubo Marine Park. == Shrine Grounds == === Main Features === * '''Main Hall (本殿)''' - Built in [[Shimmei-zukuri]] style. * '''Worship Hall (拝殿)''' - [[Gongen-zukuri]] style. * '''Sacred Ginkgo Trees''' - Planted by Minamoto no Yoritomo, the female tree's drooping branches symbolize fertility and are touched by women seeking blessings for lactation and childbirth. The male tree resembles a dragon. Designated as a Natural Monument of Miura City. === Sub-Shrines === * '''Ryūjin and Suijin Shrines''' - Sacred to water and dragon deities. * '''Hōsō Shrine''' - Dedicated to Minamoto no Tametomo, protector against disease. * '''Kōya Shrine''' - Worships Iwaka Mutsukari no Mikoto, the deity of cuisine and cooking. * '''Mitama Shrine''' - Dedicated to Kamakura Goro Kagemasa, believed to heal eye diseases. * '''Fukutoku Inari Shrine''' - For prosperity and safety in trade and fishing. * '''Konpira Shrine''' - Dedicated to Ōmononushi, a deity of maritime safety and commerce. === Notable Festivals and Rituals === * '''New Year's Eve (January 1)''' - Saitan-sai with lion dances for exorcism. * '''January 15''' - {{ill|Chakkirako}}: A unique dance registered as a UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage. * '''Summer Festival''' - Two-day event with traditional mikoshi processions. * '''Menkagura (November)''' - A traditional masked dance representing local folklore and Shinto traditions. == Access == * From '''Keikyu Kurihama Line''': - Take a bus from Miura-Kaigan Station or Misaki-guchi Station to Misaki Port (三崎港), then walk 2 minutes north. * Parking available near the shrine office. == References == {{reflist}} == See Also == * {{ill|Power spots|ja|パワースポット}} * {{ill|Minamoto no Yoritomo|ja|源頼朝}} * {{ill|Ryūjin|ja|龍神}} [[Category:Shrines in Kanagawa Prefecture]] Two days before Marine Day in July |rituals = [[Chakkirako]] (UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage) }} '''Kainan Shrine''' (海南神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Miura, Kanagawa|ja|三浦市}}, {{ill|Kanagawa Prefecture|ja|神奈川県}}, slightly inland from {{ill|Misaki Fishing Port|ja|三崎漁港}}. It is the total guardian shrine of the {{ill|Miura Peninsula|ja|三浦半島}} in {{ill|Sagami Province|ja|相模国}}, enshrining Fujiwara Sukemitsu, Mitsuwatari-hime, Senryū Benzaiten (part of the Miura Shichifukujin), and Jinushi-no-Ōkami. The shrine has a deep connection to {{ill|Minamoto no Yoritomo|ja|源頼朝}}, who revered it, and it features sacred trees planted by Yoritomo, including a dragon-shaped sacred ginkgo tree. [[Kainan Shrine]] is a regional [[Sōja (Shinto)|Sōja shrine]]. It enshrines many kami of the local region. It contrasts with provincial Soja shrines which enshrine all the kami of a provincehttps://archive.ph/wip/XtZfZ == Enshrined Deities == * '''Fujiwara Sukemitsu (藤原資盈)''' * '''Mitsuwatari-hime (盈渡姫)''' * '''Jinushi-no-Ōkami (地主大神)''' * '''Susanoo (素戔嗚尊)''' * '''{{ill|Otori-sama|ja|天日鷲神}} (天日鷲神)''' * '''Sugawara no Michizane (菅原道真)''' * '''Senryū Benzaiten (筌龍弁財天)''' == History == During the reign of {{ill|Emperor Seiwa|ja|清和天皇}}, Fujiwara Sukemitsu was exiled due to a false accusation related to a succession dispute. In {{ill|Jōgan (era)|ja|貞観}} 6 (864 CE), Sukemitsu was shipwrecked on the {{ill|Miura Peninsula|ja|三浦半島}} while traveling to his post in {{ill|Tsukushi Province|ja|筑紫国}}. The locals revered Sukemitsu for his efforts in quelling pirates and improving welfare. After his death in Jōgan 8 (866 CE), a shrine was built to honor him. In {{ill|Tengen (era)|ja|天元}} 5 (982 CE), the current shrine building was established, and the shrine became the total guardian of {{ill|Miura District, Kanagawa|ja|三浦郡}}. Minamoto no Yoritomo, following his 1180 uprising, held the shrine in high regard. Legend states that Yoritomo planted a pair of sacred ginkgo trees as offerings in 1185. The shrine received the title of "Sōchinju" (総鎮守, General Guardian Shrine) of the Miura Peninsula in 1719 (Kyōhō 4). It was designated a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}} in 1873 (Meiji 6) and listed as a shrine for offering government-provided ritual offerings in 1907 (Meiji 40). The ritual {{ill|Chakkirako|ja|チャッキラコ}}, unique to the shrine, was inscribed as a UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage in 2009. The shrine's buildings were designated as Important Cultural Properties by Kanagawa Prefecture in 2011. In 2021, the shrine became the guardian of the "Animal Shichifukujin" statues from the defunct Keikyu Aburatsubo Marine Park. == Shrine Grounds == === Main Features === * '''Main Hall (本殿)''' - Built in [[Shimmei-zukuri]] style. * '''Worship Hall (拝殿)''' - [[Gongen-zukuri]] style. * '''Sacred Ginkgo Trees''' - Planted by Minamoto no Yoritomo, the female tree's drooping branches symbolize fertility and are touched by women seeking blessings for lactation and childbirth. The male tree resembles a dragon. Designated as a Natural Monument of Miura City. === Sub-Shrines === * '''Ryūjin and Suijin Shrines''' - Sacred to water and dragon deities. * '''Hōsō Shrine''' - Dedicated to Minamoto no Tametomo, protector against disease. * '''Kōya Shrine''' - Worships Iwaka Mutsukari no Mikoto, the deity of cuisine and cooking. * '''Mitama Shrine''' - Dedicated to Kamakura Goro Kagemasa, believed to heal eye diseases. * '''Fukutoku Inari Shrine''' - For prosperity and safety in trade and fishing. * '''Konpira Shrine''' - Dedicated to Ōmononushi, a deity of maritime safety and commerce. === Notable Festivals and Rituals === * '''New Year's Eve (January 1)''' - Saitan-sai with lion dances for exorcism. * '''January 15''' - {{ill|Chakkirako}}: A unique dance registered as a UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage. * '''Summer Festival''' - Two-day event with traditional mikoshi processions. * '''Menkagura (November)''' - A traditional masked dance representing local folklore and Shinto traditions. == Access == * From '''Keikyu Kurihama Line''': - Take a bus from Miura-Kaigan Station or Misaki-guchi Station to Misaki Port (三崎港), then walk 2 minutes north. * Parking available near the shrine office. == References == {{reflist}} == See Also == * {{ill|Power spots|ja|パワースポット}} * {{ill|Minamoto no Yoritomo|ja|源頼朝}} * {{ill|Ryūjin|ja|龍神}} [[Category:Shrines in Kanagawa Prefecture]] It contrasts with provincial Soja shrines which enshrine all the kami of a provincehttps://archive.ph/wip/XtZfZ == Enshrined Deities == * '''Fujiwara Sukemitsu (藤原資盈)''' * '''Mitsuwatari-hime (盈渡姫)''' * '''Jinushi-no-Ōkami (地主大神)''' * '''Susanoo (素戔嗚尊)''' * '''{{ill|Otori-sama|ja|天日鷲神}} (天日鷲神)''' * '''Sugawara no Michizane (菅原道真)''' * '''Senryū Benzaiten (筌龍弁財天)''' == History == During the reign of {{ill|Emperor Seiwa|ja|清和天皇}}, Fujiwara Sukemitsu was exiled due to a false accusation related to a succession dispute. In {{ill|Jōgan (era)|ja|貞観}} 6 (864 CE), Sukemitsu was shipwrecked on the {{ill|Miura Peninsula|ja|三浦半島}} while traveling to his post in {{ill|Tsukushi Province|ja|筑紫国}}. The locals revered Sukemitsu for his efforts in quelling pirates and improving welfare. After his death in Jōgan 8 (866 CE), a shrine was built to honor him. In {{ill|Tengen (era)|ja|天元}} 5 (982 CE), the current shrine building was established, and the shrine became the total guardian of {{ill|Miura District, Kanagawa|ja|三浦郡}}. Minamoto no Yoritomo, following his 1180 uprising, held the shrine in high regard. Legend states that Yoritomo planted a pair of sacred ginkgo trees as offerings in 1185. The shrine received the title of "Sōchinju" (総鎮守, General Guardian Shrine) of the Miura Peninsula in 1719 (Kyōhō 4). It was designated a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}} in 1873 (Meiji 6) and listed as a shrine for offering government-provided ritual offerings in 1907 (Meiji 40). The ritual {{ill|Chakkirako|ja|チャッキラコ}}, unique to the shrine, was inscribed as a UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage in 2009. The shrine's buildings were designated as Important Cultural Properties by Kanagawa Prefecture in 2011. In 2021, the shrine became the guardian of the "Animal Shichifukujin" statues from the defunct Keikyu Aburatsubo Marine Park. == Shrine Grounds == === Main Features === * '''Main Hall (本殿)''' - Built in [[Shimmei-zukuri]] style. * '''Worship Hall (拝殿)''' - [[Gongen-zukuri]] style. * '''Sacred Ginkgo Trees''' - Planted by Minamoto no Yoritomo, the female tree's drooping branches symbolize fertility and are touched by women seeking blessings for lactation and childbirth. protector against disease. * '''Kōya Shrine''' - Worships Iwaka Mutsukari no Mikoto, the deity of cuisine and cooking. * '''Mitama Shrine''' - Dedicated to Kamakura Goro Kagemasa, believed to heal eye diseases. * '''Fukutoku Inari Shrine''' - For prosperity and safety in trade and fishing. * '''Konpira Shrine''' - Dedicated to Ōmononushi, a deity of maritime safety and commerce. === Notable Cultural Heritage. * '''Summer Festival''' - Two-day event with traditional mikoshi processions. * '''Menkagura (November)''' - A traditional masked dance representing local folklore and Shinto traditions. == Access == * From '''Keikyu Kurihama Line''': - Take a bus from Miura-Kaigan Station or Misaki-guchi Station to Misaki Port (三崎港), then walk 2 minutes north. * Parking available near the protector against disease. * '''Kōya Shrine''' - Worships Iwaka Mutsukari no Mikoto, the deity of cuisine and cooking. * '''Mitama Shrine''' - Dedicated to Kamakura Goro Kagemasa, believed to heal eye diseases. * '''Fukutoku Inari Shrine''' - For prosperity and safety in trade and fishing. * '''Konpira Shrine''' - Dedicated to Ōmononushi, a deity of maritime safety and commerce. === Notable Cultural Heritage. * '''Summer Festival''' - Two-day event with traditional mikoshi processions. * '''Menkagura (November)''' - A traditional masked dance representing local folklore and Shinto traditions. == Access == * From '''Keikyu Kurihama Line''': - Take a bus from Miura-Kaigan Station or Misaki-guchi Station to Misaki Port (三崎港), then walk 2 minutes north. * Parking available near the It is the total guardian shrine of the {{ill|Miura Peninsula|ja|三浦半島}} in {{ill|Sagami Province|ja|相模国}}, enshrining Fujiwara Sukemitsu, Mitsuwatari-hime, Senryū Benzaiten (part of the Miura Shichifukujin), and Jinushi-no-Ōkami. The shrine has a deep connection to {{ill|Minamoto no Yoritomo|ja|源頼朝}}, who revered it, and it features sacred trees planted by Yoritomo, including a dragon-shaped sacred ginkgo tree. [[Kainan Shrine]] is a regional [[Sōja (Shinto)|Sōja shrine]]. It enshrines many kami of the local region. It contrasts with provincial Soja shrines which enshrine all the kami of a provincehttps://archive.ph/wip/XtZfZ == Enshrined Deities == * '''Fujiwara Sukemitsu (藤原資盈)''' * '''Mitsuwatari-hime (盈渡姫)''' * '''Jinushi-no-Ōkami (地主大神)''' * '''Susanoo (素戔嗚尊)''' * '''{{ill|Otori-sama|ja|天日鷲神}} (天日鷲神)''' * '''Sugawara no Michizane (菅原道真)''' * '''Senryū Benzaiten (筌龍弁財天)''' == History == During the reign of {{ill|Emperor Seiwa|ja|清和天皇}}, Fujiwara Sukemitsu was exiled due to a false accusation related to a succession dispute. In {{ill|Jōgan (era)|ja|貞観}} 6 (864 CE), Sukemitsu was shipwrecked on the {{ill|Miura Peninsula|ja|三浦半島}} while traveling to his post in {{ill|Tsukushi Province|ja|筑紫国}}. The locals revered Sukemitsu for his efforts in quelling pirates and improving welfare. After his death in Jōgan 8 (866 CE), a shrine was built to honor him. In {{ill|Tengen (era)|ja|天元}} 5 (982 CE), the current shrine building was established, and the shrine became the total guardian of {{ill|Miura District, Kanagawa|ja|三浦郡}}. Minamoto no Yoritomo, following his 1180 uprising, held the shrine in high regard. Legend states that Yoritomo planted a pair of sacred ginkgo trees as offerings in 1185. The shrine received the title of "Sōchinju" (総鎮守, General Guardian Shrine) of the Miura Peninsula in 1719 (Kyōhō 4). It was designated a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}} in 1873 (Meiji 6) and listed as a shrine for offering government-provided ritual offerings in 1907 (Meiji 40). The ritual {{ill|Chakkirako|ja|チャッキラコ}}, unique to the shrine, was inscribed as a UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage in 2009. The shrine's buildings were designated as Important Cultural Properties by Kanagawa Prefecture in 2011. diseases. * '''Fukutoku Inari Shrine''' - For prosperity and safety in trade and fishing. * '''Konpira Shrine''' - Dedicated to Ōmononushi, a deity of maritime safety and commerce. === Notable {{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=13|frame-align=center|frame-width=280|coord={{coord|35|8|33.9|N|139|37|7.8|E}}}} |location = [[Kanagawa Prefecture|神奈川県]], [[Miura, Kanagawa|三浦市]], [[Misaki, Kanagawa|三崎]] 4丁目12-11 |position = {{coord|35|8|33.926|N|139|37|7.84|E|display=inline,title}} |enshrined_deities = * Fujiwara Sukemitsu (藤原資盈) * Mitsuwatari-hime (盈渡姫) * Senryū Benzaiten (筌龍弁財天; part of Miura Shichifukujin) * Jinushi-no-Ōkami (地主大神) |shrine_rank = Former [[Gōsha|郷社]] |established = [[Tengen (Japan)|Tengen]] 5 (982 CE) |main_hall = [[Shimmei-zukuri|神明造]] |main_festival = Summer Festival (designated Miura City Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property)
Two days before Marine Day in July |rituals = [[Chakkirako]] (UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage) }} '''Kainan Shrine''' (海南神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Miura, Kanagawa|ja|三浦市}}, {{ill|Kanagawa Prefecture|ja|神奈川県}}, slightly inland from {{ill|Misaki Fishing Port|ja|三崎漁港}}. It is the total guardian shrine of the {{ill|Miura Peninsula|ja|三浦半島}} in {{ill|Sagami Province|ja|相模国}}, enshrining Fujiwara Sukemitsu, Mitsuwatari-hime, Senryū Benzaiten (part of the Miura Shichifukujin), and Jinushi-no-Ōkami. The shrine has a deep connection to {{ill|Minamoto no Yoritomo|ja|源頼朝}}, who revered it, and it features sacred trees planted by Yoritomo, including a dragon-shaped sacred ginkgo tree. [[Kainan Shrine]] is a regional [[Sōja (Shinto)|Sōja shrine]]. It enshrines many kami of the local region. It contrasts with provincial Soja shrines which enshrine all the kami of a provincehttps://archive.ph/wip/XtZfZ == Enshrined Deities == * '''Fujiwara Sukemitsu (藤原資盈)''' * '''Mitsuwatari-hime (盈渡姫)''' * '''Jinushi-no-Ōkami (地主大神)''' * '''Susanoo (素戔嗚尊)''' * '''{{ill|Otori-sama|ja|天日鷲神}} (天日鷲神)''' * '''Sugawara no Michizane (菅原道真)''' * '''Senryū Benzaiten (筌龍弁財天)''' == History == During the reign of {{ill|Emperor Seiwa|ja|清和天皇}}, Fujiwara Sukemitsu was exiled due to a false accusation related to a succession dispute. In {{ill|Jōgan (era)|ja|貞観}} 6 (864 CE), Sukemitsu was shipwrecked on the {{ill|Miura Peninsula|ja|三浦半島}} while traveling to his post in {{ill|Tsukushi Province|ja|筑紫国}}. The locals revered Sukemitsu for his efforts in quelling pirates and improving welfare. After his death in Jōgan 8 (866 CE), a shrine was built to honor him. In {{ill|Tengen (era)|ja|天元}} 5 (982 CE), the current shrine building was established, and the shrine became the total guardian of {{ill|Miura District, Kanagawa|ja|三浦郡}}. Minamoto no Yoritomo, following his 1180 uprising, held the shrine in high regard. Legend states that Yoritomo planted a pair of sacred ginkgo trees as offerings in 1185. The shrine received the title of "Sōchinju" (総鎮守, General Guardian Shrine) of the Miura Peninsula in 1719 (Kyōhō 4). It was designated a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}} in 1873 (Meiji 6) and listed as a shrine for offering government-provided ritual offerings in 1907 (Meiji 40). The ritual {{ill|Chakkirako|ja|チャッキラコ}}, unique to the shrine, was inscribed as a UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage in 2009. The shrine's buildings were designated as Important Cultural Properties by Kanagawa Prefecture in 2011. In 2021, the shrine became the guardian of the "Animal Shichifukujin" statues from the defunct Keikyu Aburatsubo Marine Park. == Shrine Grounds == === Main Features === * '''Main Hall (本殿)''' - Built in [[Shimmei-zukuri]] style. * '''Worship Hall (拝殿)''' - [[Gongen-zukuri]] style. * '''Sacred Ginkgo Trees''' - Planted by Minamoto no Yoritomo, the female tree's drooping branches symbolize fertility and are touched by women seeking blessings for lactation and childbirth. The male tree resembles a dragon. Designated as a Natural Monument of Miura City. === Sub-Shrines === * '''Ryūjin and Suijin Shrines''' - Sacred to water and dragon deities. * '''Hōsō Shrine''' - Dedicated to Minamoto no Tametomo, protector against disease. * '''Kōya Shrine''' - Worships Iwaka Mutsukari no Mikoto, the deity of cuisine and cooking. * '''Mitama Shrine''' - Dedicated to Kamakura Goro Kagemasa, believed to heal eye diseases. * '''Fukutoku Inari Shrine''' - For prosperity and safety in trade and fishing. * '''Konpira Shrine''' - Dedicated to Ōmononushi, a deity of maritime safety and commerce. === Notable Festivals and Rituals === * '''New Year's Eve (January 1)''' - Saitan-sai with lion dances for exorcism. * '''January 15''' - {{ill|Chakkirako}}: A unique dance registered as a UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage. * '''Summer Festival''' - Two-day event with traditional mikoshi processions. * '''Menkagura (November)''' - A traditional masked dance representing local folklore and Shinto traditions. == Access == * From '''Keikyu Kurihama Line''': - Take a bus from Miura-Kaigan Station or Misaki-guchi Station to Misaki Port (三崎港), then walk 2 minutes north. * Parking available near the shrine office. == References == {{reflist}} == See Also == * {{ill|Power spots|ja|パワースポット}} * {{ill|Minamoto no Yoritomo|ja|源頼朝}} * {{ill|Ryūjin|ja|龍神}} [[Category:Shrines in Kanagawa Prefecture]] Haiden
{{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=13|frame-align=center|frame-width=280|coord={{coord|35|8|33.9|N|139|37|7.8|E}}}} |location = [[Kanagawa Prefecture|神奈川県]], [[Miura, Kanagawa|三浦市]], [[Misaki, Kanagawa|三崎]] 4丁目12-11 |position = {{coord|35|8|33.926|N|139|37|7.84|E|display=inline,title}} |enshrined_deities = * Fujiwara Sukemitsu (藤原資盈) * Mitsuwatari-hime (盈渡姫) * Senryū Benzaiten (筌龍弁財天; part of Miura Shichifukujin) * Jinushi-no-Ōkami (地主大神) |shrine_rank = Former [[Gōsha|郷社]] |established = [[Tengen (Japan)|Tengen]] 5 (982 CE) |main_hall = [[Shimmei-zukuri|神明造]] |main_festival = Summer Festival (designated Miura City Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property)
Two days before Marine Day in July |rituals = [[Chakkirako]] (UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage) }} '''Kainan Shrine''' (海南神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Miura, Kanagawa|ja|三浦市}}, {{ill|Kanagawa Prefecture|ja|神奈川県}}, slightly inland from {{ill|Misaki Fishing Port|ja|三崎漁港}}. It is the total guardian shrine of the {{ill|Miura Peninsula|ja|三浦半島}} in {{ill|Sagami Province|ja|相模国}}, enshrining Fujiwara Sukemitsu, Mitsuwatari-hime, Senryū Benzaiten (part of the Miura Shichifukujin), and Jinushi-no-Ōkami. The shrine has a deep connection to {{ill|Minamoto no Yoritomo|ja|源頼朝}}, who revered it, and it features sacred trees planted by Yoritomo, including a dragon-shaped sacred ginkgo tree. [[Kainan Shrine]] is a regional [[Sōja (Shinto)|Sōja shrine]]. It enshrines many kami of the local region. It contrasts with provincial Soja shrines which enshrine all the kami of a provincehttps://archive.ph/wip/XtZfZ == Enshrined Deities == * '''Fujiwara Sukemitsu (藤原資盈)''' * '''Mitsuwatari-hime (盈渡姫)''' * '''Jinushi-no-Ōkami (地主大神)''' * '''Susanoo (素戔嗚尊)''' * '''{{ill|Otori-sama|ja|天日鷲神}} (天日鷲神)''' * '''Sugawara no Michizane (菅原道真)''' * '''Senryū Benzaiten (筌龍弁財天)''' == History == During the reign of {{ill|Emperor Seiwa|ja|清和天皇}}, Fujiwara Sukemitsu was exiled due to a false accusation related to a succession dispute. In {{ill|Jōgan (era)|ja|貞観}} 6 (864 CE), Sukemitsu was shipwrecked on the {{ill|Miura Peninsula|ja|三浦半島}} while traveling to his post in {{ill|Tsukushi Province|ja|筑紫国}}. The locals revered Sukemitsu for his efforts in quelling pirates and improving welfare. After his death in Jōgan 8 (866 CE), a shrine was built to honor him. In {{ill|Tengen (era)|ja|天元}} 5 (982 CE), the current shrine building was established, and the shrine became the total guardian of {{ill|Miura District, Kanagawa|ja|三浦郡}}. Minamoto no Yoritomo, following his 1180 uprising, held the shrine in high regard. Legend states that Yoritomo planted a pair of sacred ginkgo trees as offerings in 1185. The shrine received the title of "Sōchinju" (総鎮守, General Guardian Shrine) of the Miura Peninsula in 1719 (Kyōhō 4). It was designated a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}} in 1873 (Meiji 6) and listed as a shrine for offering government-provided ritual offerings in 1907 (Meiji 40). The ritual {{ill|Chakkirako|ja|チャッキラコ}}, unique to the shrine, was inscribed as a UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage in 2009. The shrine's buildings were designated as Important Cultural Properties by Kanagawa Prefecture in 2011. In 2021, the shrine became the guardian of the "Animal Shichifukujin" statues from the defunct Keikyu Aburatsubo Marine Park. == Shrine Grounds == === Main Features === * '''Main Hall (本殿)''' - Built in [[Shimmei-zukuri]] style. * '''Worship Hall (拝殿)''' - [[Gongen-zukuri]] style. * '''Sacred Ginkgo Trees''' - Planted by Minamoto no Yoritomo, the female tree's drooping branches symbolize fertility and are touched by women seeking blessings for lactation and childbirth. The male tree resembles a dragon. Designated as a Natural Monument of Miura City. === Sub-Shrines === * '''Ryūjin and Suijin Shrines''' - Sacred to water and dragon deities. * '''Hōsō Shrine''' - Dedicated to Minamoto no Tametomo, protector against disease. * '''Kōya Shrine''' - Worships Iwaka Mutsukari no Mikoto, the deity of cuisine and cooking. * '''Mitama Shrine''' - Dedicated to Kamakura Goro Kagemasa, believed to heal eye diseases. * '''Fukutoku Inari Shrine''' - For prosperity and safety in trade and fishing. * '''Konpira Shrine''' - Dedicated to Ōmononushi, a deity of maritime safety and commerce. === Notable Festivals and Rituals === * '''New Year's Eve (January 1)''' - Saitan-sai with lion dances for exorcism. * '''January 15''' - {{ill|Chakkirako}}: A unique dance registered as a UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage. * '''Summer Festival''' - Two-day event with traditional mikoshi processions. * '''Menkagura (November)''' - A traditional masked dance representing local folklore and Shinto traditions. == Access == * From '''Keikyu Kurihama Line''': - Take a bus from Miura-Kaigan Station or Misaki-guchi Station to Misaki Port (三崎港), then walk 2 minutes north. * Parking available near the shrine office. == References == {{reflist}} == See Also == * {{ill|Power spots|ja|パワースポット}} * {{ill|Minamoto no Yoritomo|ja|源頼朝}} * {{ill|Ryūjin|ja|龍神}} [[Category:Shrines in Kanagawa Prefecture]] {{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=13|frame-align=center|frame-width=280|coord={{coord|35|8|33.9|N|139|37|7.8|E}}}} |location = [[Kanagawa Prefecture|神奈川県]], [[Miura, Kanagawa|三浦市]], [[Misaki, Kanagawa|三崎]] 4丁目12-11 |position = {{coord|35|8|33.926|N|139|37|7.84|E|display=inline,title}} |enshrined_deities = * Fujiwara Sukemitsu (藤原資盈) * Mitsuwatari-hime (盈渡姫) * Senryū Benzaiten (筌龍弁財天; part of Miura Shichifukujin) * Jinushi-no-Ōkami (地主大神) |shrine_rank = Former [[Gōsha|郷社]] |established = [[Tengen (Japan)|Tengen]] 5 (982 CE) |main_hall = [[Shimmei-zukuri|神明造]] |main_festival = Summer Festival (designated Miura City Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property)
Two days before Marine Day in July |rituals = [[Chakkirako]] (UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage) }} '''Kainan Shrine''' (海南神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Miura, Kanagawa|ja|三浦市}}, {{ill|Kanagawa Prefecture|ja|神奈川県}}, slightly inland from {{ill|Misaki Fishing Port|ja|三崎漁港}}. It is the total guardian shrine of the {{ill|Miura Peninsula|ja|三浦半島}} in {{ill|Sagami Province|ja|相模国}}, enshrining Fujiwara Sukemitsu, Mitsuwatari-hime, Senryū Benzaiten (part of the Miura Shichifukujin), and Jinushi-no-Ōkami. The shrine has a deep connection to {{ill|Minamoto no Yoritomo|ja|源頼朝}}, who revered it, and it features sacred trees planted by Yoritomo, including a dragon-shaped sacred ginkgo tree. [[Kainan Shrine]] is a regional [[Sōja (Shinto)|Sōja shrine]]. It enshrines many kami of the local region. It contrasts with provincial Soja shrines which enshrine all the kami of a provincehttps://archive.ph/wip/XtZfZ == Enshrined Deities == * '''Fujiwara Sukemitsu (藤原資盈)''' * '''Mitsuwatari-hime (盈渡姫)''' * '''Jinushi-no-Ōkami (地主大神)''' * '''Susanoo (素戔嗚尊)''' * '''{{ill|Otori-sama|ja|天日鷲神}} (天日鷲神)''' * '''Sugawara no Michizane (菅原道真)''' * '''Senryū Benzaiten (筌龍弁財天)''' == History == During the reign of {{ill|Emperor Seiwa|ja|清和天皇}}, Fujiwara Sukemitsu was exiled due to a false accusation related to a succession dispute. In {{ill|Jōgan (era)|ja|貞観}} 6 (864 CE), Sukemitsu was shipwrecked on the {{ill|Miura Peninsula|ja|三浦半島}} while traveling to his post in {{ill|Tsukushi Province|ja|筑紫国}}. The locals revered Sukemitsu for his efforts in quelling pirates and improving welfare. After his death in Jōgan 8 (866 CE), a shrine was built to honor him. In {{ill|Tengen (era)|ja|天元}} 5 (982 CE), the current shrine building was established, and the shrine became the total guardian of {{ill|Miura District, Kanagawa|ja|三浦郡}}. Minamoto no Yoritomo, following his 1180 uprising, held the shrine in high regard. Legend states that Yoritomo planted a pair of sacred ginkgo trees as offerings in 1185. The shrine received the title of "Sōchinju" (総鎮守, General Guardian Shrine) of the Miura Peninsula in 1719 (Kyōhō 4). It was designated a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}} in 1873 (Meiji 6) and listed as a shrine for offering government-provided ritual offerings in 1907 (Meiji 40). The ritual {{ill|Chakkirako|ja|チャッキラコ}}, unique to the shrine, was inscribed as a UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage in 2009. The shrine's buildings were designated as Important Cultural Properties by Kanagawa Prefecture in 2011. In 2021, the shrine became the guardian of the "Animal Shichifukujin" statues from the defunct Keikyu Aburatsubo Marine Park. == Shrine Grounds == === Main Features === * '''Main Hall (本殿)''' - Built in [[Shimmei-zukuri]] style. * '''Worship Hall (拝殿)''' - [[Gongen-zukuri]] style. * '''Sacred Ginkgo Trees''' - Planted by Minamoto no Yoritomo, the female tree's drooping branches symbolize fertility and are touched by women seeking blessings for lactation and childbirth. The male tree resembles a dragon. Designated as a Natural Monument of Miura City. === Sub-Shrines === * '''Ryūjin and Suijin Shrines''' - Sacred to water and dragon deities. * '''Hōsō Shrine''' - Dedicated to Minamoto no Tametomo, protector against disease. * '''Kōya Shrine''' - Worships Iwaka Mutsukari no Mikoto, the deity of cuisine and cooking. * '''Mitama Shrine''' - Dedicated to Kamakura Goro Kagemasa, believed to heal eye diseases. * '''Fukutoku Inari Shrine''' - For prosperity and safety in trade and fishing. * '''Konpira Shrine''' - Dedicated to Ōmononushi, a deity of maritime safety and commerce. === Notable Festivals and Rituals === * '''New Year's Eve (January 1)''' - Saitan-sai with lion dances for exorcism. * '''January 15''' - {{ill|Chakkirako}}: A unique dance registered as a UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage. * '''Summer Festival''' - Two-day event with traditional mikoshi processions. * '''Menkagura (November)''' - A traditional masked dance representing local folklore and Shinto traditions. == Access == * From '''Keikyu Kurihama Line''': - Take a bus from Miura-Kaigan Station or Misaki-guchi Station to Misaki Port (三崎港), then walk 2 minutes north. * Parking available near the shrine office. == References == {{reflist}} == See Also == * {{ill|Power spots|ja|パワースポット}} * {{ill|Minamoto no Yoritomo|ja|源頼朝}} * {{ill|Ryūjin|ja|龍神}} [[Category:Shrines in Kanagawa Prefecture]] Two days before Marine Day in July |rituals = [[Chakkirako]] (UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage) }} '''Kainan Shrine''' (海南神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Miura, Kanagawa|ja|三浦市}}, {{ill|Kanagawa Prefecture|ja|神奈川県}}, slightly inland from {{ill|Misaki Fishing Port|ja|三崎漁港}}. It is the total guardian shrine of the {{ill|Miura Peninsula|ja|三浦半島}} in {{ill|Sagami Province|ja|相模国}}, enshrining Fujiwara Sukemitsu, Mitsuwatari-hime, Senryū Benzaiten (part of the Miura Shichifukujin), and Jinushi-no-Ōkami. The shrine has a deep connection to {{ill|Minamoto no Yoritomo|ja|源頼朝}}, who revered it, and it features sacred trees planted by Yoritomo, including a dragon-shaped sacred ginkgo tree. [[Kainan Shrine]] is a regional [[Sōja (Shinto)|Sōja shrine]]. It enshrines many kami of the local region. It contrasts with provincial Soja shrines which enshrine all the kami of a provincehttps://archive.ph/wip/XtZfZ == Enshrined Deities == * '''Fujiwara Sukemitsu (藤原資盈)''' * '''Mitsuwatari-hime (盈渡姫)''' * '''Jinushi-no-Ōkami (地主大神)''' * '''Susanoo (素戔嗚尊)''' * '''{{ill|Otori-sama|ja|天日鷲神}} (天日鷲神)''' * '''Sugawara no Michizane (菅原道真)''' * '''Senryū Benzaiten (筌龍弁財天)''' == History == During the reign of {{ill|Emperor Seiwa|ja|清和天皇}}, Fujiwara Sukemitsu was exiled due to a false accusation related to a succession dispute. In {{ill|Jōgan (era)|ja|貞観}} 6 (864 CE), Sukemitsu was shipwrecked on the {{ill|Miura Peninsula|ja|三浦半島}} while traveling to his post in {{ill|Tsukushi Province|ja|筑紫国}}. The locals revered Sukemitsu for his efforts in quelling pirates and improving welfare. After his death in Jōgan 8 (866 CE), a shrine was built to honor him. In {{ill|Tengen (era)|ja|天元}} 5 (982 CE), the current shrine building was established, and the shrine became the total guardian of {{ill|Miura District, Kanagawa|ja|三浦郡}}. Minamoto no Yoritomo, following his 1180 uprising, held the shrine in high regard. Legend states that Yoritomo planted a pair of sacred ginkgo trees as offerings in 1185. The shrine received the title of "Sōchinju" (総鎮守, General Guardian Shrine) of the Miura Peninsula in 1719 (Kyōhō 4). It was designated a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}} in 1873 (Meiji 6) and listed as a shrine for offering government-provided ritual offerings in 1907 (Meiji 40). The ritual {{ill|Chakkirako|ja|チャッキラコ}}, unique to the shrine, was inscribed as a UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage in 2009. The shrine's buildings were designated as Important Cultural Properties by Kanagawa Prefecture in 2011. In 2021, the shrine became the guardian of the "Animal Shichifukujin" statues from the defunct Keikyu Aburatsubo Marine Park. == Shrine Grounds == === Main Features === * '''Main Hall (本殿)''' - Built in [[Shimmei-zukuri]] style. * '''Worship Hall (拝殿)''' - [[Gongen-zukuri]] style. * '''Sacred Ginkgo Trees''' - Planted by Minamoto no Yoritomo, the female tree's drooping branches symbolize fertility and are touched by women seeking blessings for lactation and childbirth. The male tree resembles a dragon. Designated as a Natural Monument of Miura City. === Sub-Shrines === * '''Ryūjin and Suijin Shrines''' - Sacred to water and dragon deities. * '''Hōsō Shrine''' - Dedicated to Minamoto no Tametomo, protector against disease. * '''Kōya Shrine''' - Worships Iwaka Mutsukari no Mikoto, the deity of cuisine and cooking. * '''Mitama Shrine''' - Dedicated to Kamakura Goro Kagemasa, believed to heal eye diseases. * '''Fukutoku Inari Shrine''' - For prosperity and safety in trade and fishing. * '''Konpira Shrine''' - Dedicated to Ōmononushi, a deity of maritime safety and commerce. === Notable Festivals and Rituals === * '''New Year's Eve (January 1)''' - Saitan-sai with lion dances for exorcism. * '''January 15''' - {{ill|Chakkirako}}: A unique dance registered as a UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage. * '''Summer Festival''' - Two-day event with traditional mikoshi processions. * '''Menkagura (November)''' - A traditional masked dance representing local folklore and Shinto traditions. == Access == * From '''Keikyu Kurihama Line''': - Take a bus from Miura-Kaigan Station or Misaki-guchi Station to Misaki Port (三崎港), then walk 2 minutes north. * Parking available near the shrine office. == References == {{reflist}} == See Also == * {{ill|Power spots|ja|パワースポット}} * {{ill|Minamoto no Yoritomo|ja|源頼朝}} * {{ill|Ryūjin|ja|龍神}} [[Category:Shrines in Kanagawa Prefecture]] Two days before Marine Day in July |rituals = [[Chakkirako]] (UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage) }} '''Kainan Shrine''' (海南神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Miura, Kanagawa|ja|三浦市}}, {{ill|Kanagawa Prefecture|ja|神奈川県}}, slightly inland from {{ill|Misaki Fishing Port|ja|三崎漁港}}. It is the total guardian shrine of the {{ill|Miura Peninsula|ja|三浦半島}} in {{ill|Sagami Province|ja|相模国}}, enshrining Fujiwara Sukemitsu, Mitsuwatari-hime, Senryū Benzaiten (part of the Miura Shichifukujin), and Jinushi-no-Ōkami. The shrine has a deep connection to {{ill|Minamoto no Yoritomo|ja|源頼朝}}, who revered it, and it features sacred trees planted by Yoritomo, including a dragon-shaped sacred ginkgo tree. [[Kainan Shrine]] is a regional [[Sōja (Shinto)|Sōja shrine]]. It enshrines many kami of the local region. It contrasts with provincial Soja shrines which enshrine all the kami of a provincehttps://archive.ph/wip/XtZfZ == Enshrined Deities == * '''Fujiwara Sukemitsu (藤原資盈)''' * '''Mitsuwatari-hime (盈渡姫)''' * '''Jinushi-no-Ōkami (地主大神)''' * '''Susanoo (素戔嗚尊)''' * '''{{ill|Otori-sama|ja|天日鷲神}} (天日鷲神)''' * '''Sugawara no Michizane (菅原道真)''' * '''Senryū Benzaiten (筌龍弁財天)''' == History == During the reign of {{ill|Emperor Seiwa|ja|清和天皇}}, Fujiwara Sukemitsu was exiled due to a false accusation related to a succession dispute. In {{ill|Jōgan (era)|ja|貞観}} 6 (864 CE), Sukemitsu was shipwrecked on the {{ill|Miura Peninsula|ja|三浦半島}} while traveling to his post in {{ill|Tsukushi Province|ja|筑紫国}}. The locals revered Sukemitsu for his efforts in quelling pirates and improving welfare. After his death in Jōgan 8 (866 CE), a shrine was built to honor him. In {{ill|Tengen (era)|ja|天元}} 5 (982 CE), the current shrine building was established, and the shrine became the total guardian of {{ill|Miura District, Kanagawa|ja|三浦郡}}. Minamoto no Yoritomo, following his 1180 uprising, held the shrine in high regard. Legend states that Yoritomo planted a pair of sacred ginkgo trees as offerings in 1185. The shrine received the title of "Sōchinju" (総鎮守, General Guardian Shrine) of the Miura Peninsula in 1719 (Kyōhō 4). It was designated a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}} in 1873 (Meiji 6) and listed as a shrine for offering government-provided ritual offerings in 1907 (Meiji 40). The ritual {{ill|Chakkirako|ja|チャッキラコ}}, unique to the shrine, was inscribed as a UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage in 2009. The shrine's buildings were designated as Important Cultural Properties by Kanagawa Prefecture in 2011. In 2021, the shrine became the guardian of the "Animal Shichifukujin" statues from the defunct Keikyu Aburatsubo Marine Park. == Shrine Grounds == === Main Features === * '''Main Hall (本殿)''' - Built in [[Shimmei-zukuri]] style. * '''Worship Hall (拝殿)''' - [[Gongen-zukuri]] style. * '''Sacred Ginkgo Trees''' - Planted by Minamoto no Yoritomo, the female tree's drooping branches symbolize fertility and are touched by women seeking blessings for lactation and childbirth. The male tree resembles a dragon. Designated as a Natural Monument of Miura City. === Sub-Shrines === * '''Ryūjin and Suijin Shrines''' - Sacred to water and dragon deities. * '''Hōsō Shrine''' - Dedicated to Minamoto no Tametomo, protector against disease. * '''Kōya Shrine''' - Worships Iwaka Mutsukari no Mikoto, the deity of cuisine and cooking. * '''Mitama Shrine''' - Dedicated to Kamakura Goro Kagemasa, believed to heal eye diseases. * '''Fukutoku Inari Shrine''' - For prosperity and safety in trade and fishing. * '''Konpira Shrine''' - Dedicated to Ōmononushi, a deity of maritime safety and commerce. === Notable Festivals and Rituals === * '''New Year's Eve (January 1)''' - Saitan-sai with lion dances for exorcism. * '''January 15''' - {{ill|Chakkirako}}: A unique dance registered as a UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage. * '''Summer Festival''' - Two-day event with traditional mikoshi processions. * '''Menkagura (November)''' - A traditional masked dance representing local folklore and Shinto traditions. == Access == * From '''Keikyu Kurihama Line''': - Take a bus from Miura-Kaigan Station or Misaki-guchi Station to Misaki Port (三崎港), then walk 2 minutes north. * Parking available near the shrine office. == References == {{reflist}} == See Also == * {{ill|Power spots|ja|パワースポット}} * {{ill|Minamoto no Yoritomo|ja|源頼朝}} * {{ill|Ryūjin|ja|龍神}} [[Category:Shrines in Kanagawa Prefecture]] It is the total guardian shrine of the {{ill|Miura Peninsula|ja|三浦半島}} in {{ill|Sagami Province|ja|相模国}}, enshrining Fujiwara Sukemitsu, Mitsuwatari-hime, Senryū Benzaiten (part of the Miura Shichifukujin), and Jinushi-no-Ōkami. The shrine has a deep connection to {{ill|Minamoto no Yoritomo|ja|源頼朝}}, who revered it, and it features sacred trees planted by Yoritomo, including a dragon-shaped sacred ginkgo tree. [[Kainan Shrine]] is a regional [[Sōja (Shinto)|Sōja shrine]]. It enshrines many kami of the local region. It contrasts with provincial Soja shrines which enshrine all the kami of a provincehttps://archive.ph/wip/XtZfZ == Enshrined Deities == * '''Fujiwara Sukemitsu (藤原資盈)''' * '''Mitsuwatari-hime (盈渡姫)''' * '''Jinushi-no-Ōkami (地主大神)''' * '''Susanoo (素戔嗚尊)''' * '''{{ill|Otori-sama|ja|天日鷲神}} (天日鷲神)''' * '''Sugawara no Michizane (菅原道真)''' * '''Senryū Benzaiten (筌龍弁財天)''' == History == During the reign of {{ill|Emperor Seiwa|ja|清和天皇}}, Fujiwara Sukemitsu was exiled due to a false accusation related to a succession dispute. In {{ill|Jōgan (era)|ja|貞観}} 6 (864 CE), Sukemitsu was shipwrecked on the {{ill|Miura Peninsula|ja|三浦半島}} while traveling to his post in {{ill|Tsukushi Province|ja|筑紫国}}. The locals revered Sukemitsu for his efforts in quelling pirates and improving welfare. After his death in Jōgan 8 (866 CE), a shrine was built to honor him. In {{ill|Tengen (era)|ja|天元}} 5 (982 CE), the current shrine building was established, and the shrine became the total guardian of {{ill|Miura District, Kanagawa|ja|三浦郡}}. Minamoto no Yoritomo, following his 1180 uprising, held the shrine in high regard. Legend states that Yoritomo planted a pair of sacred ginkgo trees as offerings in 1185. The shrine received the title of "Sōchinju" (総鎮守, General Guardian Shrine) of the Miura Peninsula in 1719 (Kyōhō 4). It was designated a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}} in 1873 (Meiji 6) and listed as a shrine for offering government-provided ritual offerings in 1907 (Meiji 40). The ritual {{ill|Chakkirako|ja|チャッキラコ}}, unique to the shrine, was inscribed as a UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage in 2009. The shrine's buildings were designated as Important Cultural Properties by Kanagawa Prefecture in 2011. In 2021, the shrine became the guardian of the "Animal Shichifukujin" statues from the defunct Keikyu Aburatsubo Marine Park. == Shrine Grounds == === Main Features === * '''Main Hall (本殿)''' - Built in [[Shimmei-zukuri]] style. * '''Worship Hall (拝殿)''' - [[Gongen-zukuri]] style. * '''Sacred Ginkgo Trees''' - Planted by Minamoto no Yoritomo, the female tree's drooping branches symbolize fertility and are touched by women seeking blessings for lactation and childbirth. The male tree resembles a dragon. Designated as a Natural Monument of Miura City. === Sub-Shrines === * '''Ryūjin and Suijin Shrines''' - Sacred to water and dragon deities. * '''Hōsō Shrine''' - Dedicated to Minamoto no Tametomo, protector against disease. * '''Kōya Shrine''' - Worships Iwaka Mutsukari no Mikoto, the deity of cuisine and cooking. * '''Mitama Shrine''' - Dedicated to Kamakura Goro Kagemasa, believed to heal eye diseases. * '''Fukutoku Inari Shrine''' - For prosperity and safety in trade and fishing. * '''Konpira Shrine''' - Dedicated to Ōmononushi, a deity of maritime safety and commerce. === Notable Festivals and Rituals === * '''New Year's Eve (January 1)''' - Saitan-sai with lion dances for exorcism. * '''January 15''' - {{ill|Chakkirako}}: A unique dance registered as a UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage. * '''Summer Festival''' - Two-day event with traditional mikoshi processions. * '''Menkagura (November)''' - A traditional masked dance representing local folklore and Shinto traditions. == Access == * From '''Keikyu Kurihama Line''': - Take a bus from Miura-Kaigan Station or Misaki-guchi Station to Misaki Port (三崎港), then walk 2 minutes north. * Parking available near the shrine office. == References == {{reflist}} == See Also == * {{ill|Power spots|ja|パワースポット}} * {{ill|Minamoto no Yoritomo|ja|源頼朝}} * {{ill|Ryūjin|ja|龍神}} [[Category:Shrines in Kanagawa Prefecture]] It contrasts with provincial Soja shrines which enshrine all the kami of a provincehttps://archive.ph/wip/XtZfZ == Enshrined Deities == * '''Fujiwara Sukemitsu (藤原資盈)''' * '''Mitsuwatari-hime (盈渡姫)''' * '''Jinushi-no-Ōkami (地主大神)''' * '''Susanoo (素戔嗚尊)''' * '''{{ill|Otori-sama|ja|天日鷲神}} (天日鷲神)''' * '''Sugawara no Michizane (菅原道真)''' * '''Senryū Benzaiten (筌龍弁財天)''' == History == During the reign of {{ill|Emperor Seiwa|ja|清和天皇}}, Fujiwara Sukemitsu was exiled due to a false accusation related to a succession dispute. In {{ill|Jōgan (era)|ja|貞観}} 6 (864 CE), Sukemitsu was shipwrecked on the {{ill|Miura Peninsula|ja|三浦半島}} while traveling to his post in {{ill|Tsukushi Province|ja|筑紫国}}. The locals revered Sukemitsu for his efforts in quelling pirates and improving welfare. After his death in Jōgan 8 (866 CE), a shrine was built to honor him. In {{ill|Tengen (era)|ja|天元}} 5 (982 CE), the current shrine building was established, and the shrine became the total guardian of {{ill|Miura District, Kanagawa|ja|三浦郡}}. Minamoto no Yoritomo, following his 1180 uprising, held the shrine in high regard. Legend states that Yoritomo planted a pair of sacred ginkgo trees as offerings in 1185. The shrine received the title of "Sōchinju" (総鎮守, General Guardian Shrine) of the Miura Peninsula in 1719 (Kyōhō 4). It was designated a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}} in 1873 (Meiji 6) and listed as a shrine for offering government-provided ritual offerings in 1907 (Meiji 40). The ritual {{ill|Chakkirako|ja|チャッキラコ}}, unique to the shrine, was inscribed as a UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage in 2009. The shrine's buildings were designated as Important Cultural Properties by Kanagawa Prefecture in 2011. In 2021, the shrine became the guardian of the "Animal Shichifukujin" statues from the defunct Keikyu Aburatsubo Marine Park. == Shrine Grounds == === Main Features === * '''Main Hall (本殿)''' - Built in [[Shimmei-zukuri]] style. * '''Worship Hall (拝殿)''' - [[Gongen-zukuri]] style. * '''Sacred Ginkgo Trees''' - Planted by Minamoto no Yoritomo, the female tree's drooping branches symbolize fertility and are touched by women seeking blessings for lactation and childbirth. The male tree resembles a dragon. Designated as a Natural Monument of Miura City. === Sub-Shrines === * '''Ryūjin and Suijin Shrines''' - Sacred to water and dragon deities. * '''Hōsō Shrine''' - Dedicated to Minamoto no Tametomo, protector against disease. * '''Kōya Shrine''' - Worships Iwaka Mutsukari no Mikoto, the deity of cuisine and cooking. * '''Mitama Shrine''' - Dedicated to Kamakura Goro Kagemasa, believed to heal eye diseases. * '''Fukutoku Inari Shrine''' - For prosperity and safety in trade and fishing. * '''Konpira Shrine''' - Dedicated to Ōmononushi, a deity of maritime safety and commerce. === Notable Cultural Heritage. * '''Summer Festival''' - Two-day event with traditional mikoshi processions. * '''Menkagura (November)''' - A traditional masked dance representing local folklore and Shinto traditions. == Access == * From '''Keikyu Kurihama Line''': - Take a bus from Miura-Kaigan Station or Misaki-guchi Station to Misaki Port (三崎港), then walk 2 minutes north. * Parking available near the {{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=13|frame-align=center|frame-width=280|coord={{coord|35|8|33.9|N|139|37|7.8|E}}}} |location = [[Kanagawa Prefecture|神奈川県]], [[Miura, Kanagawa|三浦市]], [[Misaki, Kanagawa|三崎]] 4丁目12-11 |position = {{coord|35|8|33.926|N|139|37|7.84|E|display=inline,title}} |enshrined_deities = * Fujiwara Sukemitsu (藤原資盈) * Mitsuwatari-hime (盈渡姫) * Senryū Benzaiten (筌龍弁財天; part of Miura Shichifukujin) * Jinushi-no-Ōkami (地主大神) |shrine_rank = Former [[Gōsha|郷社]] |established = [[Tengen (Japan)|Tengen]] 5 (982 CE) |main_hall = [[Shimmei-zukuri|神明造]] |main_festival = Summer Festival (designated Miura City Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property)
Two days before Marine Day in July |rituals = [[Chakkirako]] (UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage) }} '''Kainan Shrine''' (海南神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Miura, Kanagawa|ja|三浦市}}, {{ill|Kanagawa Prefecture|ja|神奈川県}}, slightly inland from {{ill|Misaki Fishing Port|ja|三崎漁港}}. It is the total guardian shrine of the {{ill|Miura Peninsula|ja|三浦半島}} in {{ill|Sagami Province|ja|相模国}}, enshrining Fujiwara Sukemitsu, Mitsuwatari-hime, Senryū Benzaiten (part of the Miura Shichifukujin), and Jinushi-no-Ōkami. The shrine has a deep connection to {{ill|Minamoto no Yoritomo|ja|源頼朝}}, who revered it, and it features sacred trees planted by Yoritomo, including a dragon-shaped sacred ginkgo tree. [[Kainan Shrine]] is a regional [[Sōja (Shinto)|Sōja shrine]]. It enshrines many kami of the local region. It contrasts with provincial Soja shrines which enshrine all the kami of a provincehttps://archive.ph/wip/XtZfZ == Enshrined Deities == * '''Fujiwara Sukemitsu (藤原資盈)''' * '''Mitsuwatari-hime (盈渡姫)''' * '''Jinushi-no-Ōkami (地主大神)''' * '''Susanoo (素戔嗚尊)''' * '''{{ill|Otori-sama|ja|天日鷲神}} (天日鷲神)''' * '''Sugawara no Michizane (Sugawara no Michizane)''' * '''Senryū Benzaiten (筌龍弁財天)''' == History == During the reign of {{ill|Emperor Seiwa|ja|清和天皇}}, Fujiwara Sukemitsu was exiled due to a false accusation related to a succession dispute. In {{ill|Jōgan (era)|ja|貞観}} 6 (864 CE), Sukemitsu was shipwrecked on the {{ill|Miura Peninsula|ja|三浦半島}} while traveling to his post in {{ill|Tsukushi Province|ja|筑紫国}}. The locals revered Sukemitsu for his efforts in quelling pirates and improving welfare. After his death in Jōgan 8 (866 CE), a shrine was built to honor him. In {{ill|Tengen (era)|ja|天元}} 5 (982 CE), the current shrine building was established, and the shrine became the total guardian of {{ill|Miura District, Kanagawa|ja|三浦郡}}. Minamoto no Yoritomo, following his 1180 uprising, held the shrine in high regard. Legend states that Yoritomo planted a pair of sacred ginkgo trees as offerings in 1185. The shrine received the title of "Sōchinju" (総鎮守, General Guardian Shrine) of the Miura Peninsula in 1719 (Kyōhō 4). It was designated a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}} in 1873 (Meiji 6) and listed as a shrine for offering government-provided ritual offerings in 1907 (Meiji 40). The ritual {{ill|Chakkirako|ja|チャッキラコ}}, unique to the shrine, was inscribed as a UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage in 2009. The shrine's buildings were designated as Important Cultural Properties by Kanagawa Prefecture in 2011. In 2021, the shrine became the guardian of the "Animal Shichifukujin" statues from the defunct Keikyu Aburatsubo Marine Park. == Shrine Grounds == === Main Features === * '''Main Hall (本殿)''' - Built in [[Shimmei-zukuri]] style. * '''Worship Hall (拝殿)''' - [[Gongen-zukuri]] style. * '''Sacred Ginkgo Trees''' - Planted by Minamoto no Yoritomo, the female tree's drooping branches symbolize fertility and are touched by women seeking blessings for lactation and childbirth. The male tree resembles a dragon. Designated as a Natural Monument of Miura City. === Sub-Shrines === * '''Ryūjin and Suijin Shrines''' - Sacred to water and dragon deities. * '''Hōsō Shrine''' - Dedicated to Minamoto no Tametomo, protector against disease. * '''Kōya Shrine''' - Worships Iwaka Mutsukari no Mikoto, the deity of cuisine and cooking. * '''Mitama Shrine''' - Dedicated to Kamakura Goro Kagemasa, believed to heal eye diseases. * '''Fukutoku Inari Shrine''' - For prosperity and safety in trade and fishing. * '''Konpira Shrine''' - Dedicated to Ōmononushi, a deity of maritime safety and commerce. === Notable Festivals and Rituals === * '''New Year's Eve (January 1)''' - Saitan-sai with lion dances for exorcism. * '''January 15''' - {{ill|Chakkirako}}: A unique dance registered as a UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage. * '''Summer Festival''' - Two-day event with traditional mikoshi processions. * '''Menkagura (November)''' - A traditional masked dance representing local folklore and Shinto traditions. == Access == * From '''Keikyu Kurihama Line''': - Take a bus from Miura-Kaigan Station or Misaki-guchi Station to Misaki Port (三崎港), then walk 2 minutes north. * Parking available near the shrine office. == References == {{reflist}} == See Also == * {{ill|Power spots|ja|パワースポット}} * {{ill|Minamoto no Yoritomo|ja|源頼朝}} * {{ill|Ryūjin|ja|龍神}} [[Category:Shrines in Kanagawa Prefecture]] Haiden
{{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=13|frame-align=center|frame-width=280|coord={{coord|35|8|33.9|N|139|37|7.8|E}}}} |location = [[Kanagawa Prefecture|神奈川県]], [[Miura, Kanagawa|三浦市]], [[Misaki, Kanagawa|三崎]] 4丁目12-11 |position = {{coord|35|8|33.926|N|139|37|7.84|E|display=inline,title}} |enshrined_deities = * Fujiwara Sukemitsu (藤原資盈) * Mitsuwatari-hime (盈渡姫) * Senryū Benzaiten (筌龍弁財天; part of Miura Shichifukujin) * Jinushi-no-Ōkami (地主大神) |shrine_rank = Former [[Gōsha|郷社]] |established = [[Tengen (Japan)|Tengen]] 5 (982 CE) |main_hall = [[Shimmei-zukuri|神明造]] |main_festival = Summer Festival (designated Miura City Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property)
Two days before Marine Day in July |rituals = [[Chakkirako]] (UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage) }} '''Kainan Shrine''' (海南神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Miura, Kanagawa|ja|三浦市}}, {{ill|Kanagawa Prefecture|ja|神奈川県}}, slightly inland from {{ill|Misaki Fishing Port|ja|三崎漁港}}. It is the total guardian shrine of the {{ill|Miura Peninsula|ja|三浦半島}} in {{ill|Sagami Province|ja|相模国}}, enshrining Fujiwara Sukemitsu, Mitsuwatari-hime, Senryū Benzaiten (part of the Miura Shichifukujin), and Jinushi-no-Ōkami. The shrine has a deep connection to {{ill|Minamoto no Yoritomo|ja|源頼朝}}, who revered it, and it features sacred trees planted by Yoritomo, including a dragon-shaped sacred ginkgo tree. [[Kainan Shrine]] is a regional [[Sōja (Shinto)|Sōja shrine]]. It enshrines many kami of the local region. It contrasts with provincial Soja shrines which enshrine all the kami of a provincehttps://archive.ph/wip/XtZfZ == Enshrined Deities == * '''Fujiwara Sukemitsu (藤原資盈)''' * '''Mitsuwatari-hime (盈渡姫)''' * '''Jinushi-no-Ōkami (地主大神)''' * '''Susanoo (素戔嗚尊)''' * '''{{ill|Otori-sama|ja|天日鷲神}} (天日鷲神)''' * '''Sugawara no Michizane (Sugawara no Michizane)''' * '''Senryū Benzaiten (筌龍弁財天)''' == History == During the reign of {{ill|Emperor Seiwa|ja|清和天皇}}, Fujiwara Sukemitsu was exiled due to a false accusation related to a succession dispute. In {{ill|Jōgan (era)|ja|貞観}} 6 (864 CE), Sukemitsu was shipwrecked on the {{ill|Miura Peninsula|ja|三浦半島}} while traveling to his post in {{ill|Tsukushi Province|ja|筑紫国}}. The locals revered Sukemitsu for his efforts in quelling pirates and improving welfare. After his death in Jōgan 8 (866 CE), a shrine was built to honor him. In {{ill|Tengen (era)|ja|天元}} 5 (982 CE), the current shrine building was established, and the shrine became the total guardian of {{ill|Miura District, Kanagawa|ja|三浦郡}}. Minamoto no Yoritomo, following his 1180 uprising, held the shrine in high regard. Legend states that Yoritomo planted a pair of sacred ginkgo trees as offerings in 1185. The shrine received the title of "Sōchinju" (総鎮守, General Guardian Shrine) of the Miura Peninsula in 1719 (Kyōhō 4). It was designated a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}} in 1873 (Meiji 6) and listed as a shrine for offering government-provided ritual offerings in 1907 (Meiji 40). The ritual {{ill|Chakkirako|ja|チャッキラコ}}, unique to the shrine, was inscribed as a UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage in 2009. The shrine's buildings were designated as Important Cultural Properties by Kanagawa Prefecture in 2011. In 2021, the shrine became the guardian of the "Animal Shichifukujin" statues from the defunct Keikyu Aburatsubo Marine Park. == Shrine Grounds == === Main Features === * '''Main Hall (本殿)''' - Built in [[Shimmei-zukuri]] style. * '''Worship Hall (拝殿)''' - [[Gongen-zukuri]] style. * '''Sacred Ginkgo Trees''' - Planted by Minamoto no Yoritomo, the female tree's drooping branches symbolize fertility and are touched by women seeking blessings for lactation and childbirth. The male tree resembles a dragon. Designated as a Natural Monument of Miura City. === Sub-Shrines === * '''Ryūjin and Suijin Shrines''' - Sacred to water and dragon deities. * '''Hōsō Shrine''' - Dedicated to Minamoto no Tametomo, protector against disease. * '''Kōya Shrine''' - Worships Iwaka Mutsukari no Mikoto, the deity of cuisine and cooking. * '''Mitama Shrine''' - Dedicated to Kamakura Goro Kagemasa, believed to heal eye diseases. * '''Fukutoku Inari Shrine''' - For prosperity and safety in trade and fishing. * '''Konpira Shrine''' - Dedicated to Ōmononushi, a deity of maritime safety and commerce. === Notable Festivals and Rituals === * '''New Year's Eve (January 1)''' - Saitan-sai with lion dances for exorcism. * '''January 15''' - {{ill|Chakkirako}}: A unique dance registered as a UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage. * '''Summer Festival''' - Two-day event with traditional mikoshi processions. * '''Menkagura (November)''' - A traditional masked dance representing local folklore and Shinto traditions. == Access == * From '''Keikyu Kurihama Line''': - Take a bus from Miura-Kaigan Station or Misaki-guchi Station to Misaki Port (三崎港), then walk 2 minutes north. * Parking available near the shrine office. == References == {{reflist}} == See Also == * {{ill|Power spots|ja|パワースポット}} * {{ill|Minamoto no Yoritomo|ja|源頼朝}} * {{ill|Ryūjin|ja|龍神}} [[Category:Shrines in Kanagawa Prefecture]] Haiden
{{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=13|frame-align=center|frame-width=280|coord={{coord|35|8|33.9|N|139|37|7.8|E}}}} |location = [[Kanagawa Prefecture|神奈川県]], [[Miura, Kanagawa|三浦市]], [[Misaki, Kanagawa|三崎]] 4丁目12-11 |position = {{coord|35|8|33.926|N|139|37|7.84|E|display=inline,title}} |enshrined_deities = * Fujiwara Sukemitsu (藤原資盈) * Mitsuwatari-hime (盈渡姫) * Senryū Benzaiten (筌龍弁財天; part of Miura Shichifukujin) * Jinushi-no-Ōkami (地主大神) |shrine_rank = Former [[Gōsha|郷社]] |established = [[Tengen (Japan)|Tengen]] 5 (982 CE) |main_hall = [[Shimmei-zukuri|神明造]] |main_festival = Summer Festival (designated Miura City Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property)
Two days before Marine Day in July |rituals = [[Chakkirako]] (UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage) }} '''Kainan Shrine''' (海南神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Miura, Kanagawa|ja|三浦市}}, {{ill|Kanagawa Prefecture|ja|神奈川県}}, slightly inland from {{ill|Misaki Fishing Port|ja|三崎漁港}}. It is the total guardian shrine of the {{ill|Miura Peninsula|ja|三浦半島}} in {{ill|Sagami Province|ja|相模国}}, enshrining Fujiwara Sukemitsu, Mitsuwatari-hime, Senryū Benzaiten (part of the Miura Shichifukujin), and Jinushi-no-Ōkami. The shrine has a deep connection to {{ill|Minamoto no Yoritomo|ja|源頼朝}}, who revered it, and it features sacred trees planted by Yoritomo, including a dragon-shaped sacred ginkgo tree. [[Kainan Shrine]] is a regional [[Sōja (Shinto)|Sōja shrine]]. It enshrines many kami of the local region. It contrasts with provincial Soja shrines which enshrine all the kami of a provincehttps://archive.ph/wip/XtZfZ == Enshrined Deities == * '''Fujiwara Sukemitsu (藤原資盈)''' * '''Mitsuwatari-hime (盈渡姫)''' * '''Jinushi-no-Ōkami (地主大神)''' * '''Susanoo (素戔嗚尊)''' * '''{{ill|Otori-sama|ja|天日鷲神}} (天日鷲神)''' * '''Sugawara no Michizane (Sugawara no Michizane)''' * '''Senryū Benzaiten (筌龍弁財天)''' == History == During the reign of {{ill|Emperor Seiwa|ja|清和天皇}}, Fujiwara Sukemitsu was exiled due to a false accusation related to a succession dispute. In {{ill|Jōgan (era)|ja|貞観}} 6 (864 CE), Sukemitsu was shipwrecked on the {{ill|Miura Peninsula|ja|三浦半島}} while traveling to his post in {{ill|Tsukushi Province|ja|筑紫国}}. The locals revered Sukemitsu for his efforts in quelling pirates and improving welfare. After his death in Jōgan 8 (866 CE), a shrine was built to honor him. In {{ill|Tengen (era)|ja|天元}} 5 (982 CE), the current shrine building was established, and the shrine became the total guardian of {{ill|Miura District, Kanagawa|ja|三浦郡}}. Minamoto no Yoritomo, following his 1180 uprising, held the shrine in high regard. Legend states that Yoritomo planted a pair of sacred ginkgo trees as offerings in 1185. The shrine received the title of "Sōchinju" (総鎮守, General Guardian Shrine) of the Miura Peninsula in 1719 (Kyōhō 4). It was designated a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}} in 1873 (Meiji 6) and listed as a shrine for offering government-provided ritual offerings in 1907 (Meiji 40). The ritual {{ill|Chakkirako|ja|チャッキラコ}}, unique to the shrine, was inscribed as a UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage in 2009. The shrine's buildings were designated as Important Cultural Properties by Kanagawa Prefecture in 2011. In 2021, the shrine became the guardian of the "Animal Shichifukujin" statues from the defunct Keikyu Aburatsubo Marine Park. == Shrine Grounds == === Main Features === * '''Main Hall (本殿)''' - Built in [[Shimmei-zukuri]] style. * '''Worship Hall (拝殿)''' - [[Gongen-zukuri]] style. * '''Sacred Ginkgo Trees''' - Planted by Minamoto no Yoritomo, the female tree's drooping branches symbolize fertility and are touched by women seeking blessings for lactation and childbirth. The male tree resembles a dragon. Designated as a Natural Monument of Miura City. === Sub-Shrines === * '''Ryūjin and Suijin Shrines''' - Sacred to water and dragon deities. * '''Hōsō Shrine''' - Dedicated to Minamoto no Tametomo, protector against disease. * '''Kōya Shrine''' - Worships Iwaka Mutsukari no Mikoto, the deity of cuisine and cooking. * '''Mitama Shrine''' - Dedicated to Kamakura Goro Kagemasa, believed to heal eye diseases. * '''Fukutoku Inari Shrine''' - For prosperity and safety in trade and fishing. * '''Konpira Shrine''' - Dedicated to Ōmononushi, a deity of maritime safety and commerce. === Notable Festivals and Rituals === * '''New Year's Eve (January 1)''' - Saitan-sai with lion dances for exorcism. * '''January 15''' - {{ill|Chakkirako}}: A unique dance registered as a UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage. * '''Summer Festival''' - Two-day event with traditional mikoshi processions. * '''Menkagura (November)''' - A traditional masked dance representing local folklore and Shinto traditions. == Access == * From '''Keikyu Kurihama Line''': - Take a bus from Miura-Kaigan Station or Misaki-guchi Station to Misaki Port (三崎港), then walk 2 minutes north. * Parking available near the shrine office. == References == {{reflist}} == See Also == * {{ill|Power spots|ja|パワースポット}} * {{ill|Minamoto no Yoritomo|ja|源頼朝}} * {{ill|Ryūjin|ja|龍神}} [[Category:Shrines in Kanagawa Prefecture]] {{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=13|frame-align=center|frame-width=280|coord={{coord|35|8|33.9|N|139|37|7.8|E}}}} |location = [[Kanagawa Prefecture|神奈川県]], [[Miura, Kanagawa|三浦市]], [[Misaki, Kanagawa|三崎]] 4丁目12-11 |position = {{coord|35|8|33.926|N|139|37|7.84|E|display=inline,title}} |enshrined_deities = * Fujiwara Sukemitsu (藤原資盈) * Mitsuwatari-hime (盈渡姫) * Senryū Benzaiten (筌龍弁財天; part of Miura Shichifukujin) * Jinushi-no-Ōkami (地主大神) |shrine_rank = Former [[Gōsha|郷社]] |established = [[Tengen (Japan)|Tengen]] 5 (982 CE) |main_hall = [[Shimmei-zukuri|神明造]] |main_festival = Summer Festival (designated Miura City Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property)
Two days before Marine Day in July |rituals = [[Chakkirako]] (UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage) }} '''Kainan Shrine''' (海南神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Miura, Kanagawa|ja|三浦市}}, {{ill|Kanagawa Prefecture|ja|神奈川県}}, slightly inland from {{ill|Misaki Fishing Port|ja|三崎漁港}}. It is the total guardian shrine of the {{ill|Miura Peninsula|ja|三浦半島}} in {{ill|Sagami Province|ja|相模国}}, enshrining Fujiwara Sukemitsu, Mitsuwatari-hime, Senryū Benzaiten (part of the Miura Shichifukujin), and Jinushi-no-Ōkami. The shrine has a deep connection to {{ill|Minamoto no Yoritomo|ja|源頼朝}}, who revered it, and it features sacred trees planted by Yoritomo, including a dragon-shaped sacred ginkgo tree. [[Kainan Shrine]] is a regional [[Sōja (Shinto)|Sōja shrine]]. It enshrines many kami of the local region. It contrasts with provincial Soja shrines which enshrine all the kami of a provincehttps://archive.ph/wip/XtZfZ == Enshrined Deities == * '''Fujiwara Sukemitsu (藤原資盈)''' * '''Mitsuwatari-hime (盈渡姫)''' * '''Jinushi-no-Ōkami (地主大神)''' * '''Susanoo (素戔嗚尊)''' * '''{{ill|Otori-sama|ja|天日鷲神}} (天日鷲神)''' * '''Sugawara no Michizane (Sugawara no Michizane)''' * '''Senryū Benzaiten (筌龍弁財天)''' == History == During the reign of {{ill|Emperor Seiwa|ja|清和天皇}}, Fujiwara Sukemitsu was exiled due to a false accusation related to a succession dispute. In {{ill|Jōgan (era)|ja|貞観}} 6 (864 CE), Sukemitsu was shipwrecked on the {{ill|Miura Peninsula|ja|三浦半島}} while traveling to his post in {{ill|Tsukushi Province|ja|筑紫国}}. The locals revered Sukemitsu for his efforts in quelling pirates and improving welfare. After his death in Jōgan 8 (866 CE), a shrine was built to honor him. In {{ill|Tengen (era)|ja|天元}} 5 (982 CE), the current shrine building was established, and the shrine became the total guardian of {{ill|Miura District, Kanagawa|ja|三浦郡}}. Minamoto no Yoritomo, following his 1180 uprising, held the shrine in high regard. Legend states that Yoritomo planted a pair of sacred ginkgo trees as offerings in 1185. The shrine received the title of "Sōchinju" (総鎮守, General Guardian Shrine) of the Miura Peninsula in 1719 (Kyōhō 4). It was designated a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}} in 1873 (Meiji 6) and listed as a shrine for offering government-provided ritual offerings in 1907 (Meiji 40). The ritual {{ill|Chakkirako|ja|チャッキラコ}}, unique to the shrine, was inscribed as a UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage in 2009. The shrine's buildings were designated as Important Cultural Properties by Kanagawa Prefecture in 2011. In 2021, the shrine became the guardian of the "Animal Shichifukujin" statues from the defunct Keikyu Aburatsubo Marine Park. == Shrine Grounds == === Main Features === * '''Main Hall (本殿)''' - Built in [[Shimmei-zukuri]] style. * '''Worship Hall (拝殿)''' - [[Gongen-zukuri]] style. * '''Sacred Ginkgo Trees''' - Planted by Minamoto no Yoritomo, the female tree's drooping branches symbolize fertility and are touched by women seeking blessings for lactation and childbirth. The male tree resembles a dragon. Designated as a Natural Monument of Miura City. === Sub-Shrines === * '''Ryūjin and Suijin Shrines''' - Sacred to water and dragon deities. * '''Hōsō Shrine''' - Dedicated to Minamoto no Tametomo, protector against disease. * '''Kōya Shrine''' - Worships Iwaka Mutsukari no Mikoto, the deity of cuisine and cooking. * '''Mitama Shrine''' - Dedicated to Kamakura Goro Kagemasa, believed to heal eye diseases. * '''Fukutoku Inari Shrine''' - For prosperity and safety in trade and fishing. * '''Konpira Shrine''' - Dedicated to Ōmononushi, a deity of maritime safety and commerce. === Notable Festivals and Rituals === * '''New Year's Eve (January 1)''' - Saitan-sai with lion dances for exorcism. * '''January 15''' - {{ill|Chakkirako}}: A unique dance registered as a UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage. * '''Summer Festival''' - Two-day event with traditional mikoshi processions. * '''Menkagura (November)''' - A traditional masked dance representing local folklore and Shinto traditions. == Access == * From '''Keikyu Kurihama Line''': - Take a bus from Miura-Kaigan Station or Misaki-guchi Station to Misaki Port (三崎港), then walk 2 minutes north. * Parking available near the shrine office. == References == {{reflist}} == See Also == * {{ill|Power spots|ja|パワースポット}} * {{ill|Minamoto no Yoritomo|ja|源頼朝}} * {{ill|Ryūjin|ja|龍神}} [[Category:Shrines in Kanagawa Prefecture]] Two days before Marine Day in July |rituals = [[Chakkirako]] (UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage) }} '''Kainan Shrine''' (海南神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Miura, Kanagawa|ja|三浦市}}, {{ill|Kanagawa Prefecture|ja|神奈川県}}, slightly inland from {{ill|Misaki Fishing Port|ja|三崎漁港}}. It is the total guardian shrine of the {{ill|Miura Peninsula|ja|三浦半島}} in {{ill|Sagami Province|ja|相模国}}, enshrining Fujiwara Sukemitsu, Mitsuwatari-hime, Senryū Benzaiten (part of the Miura Shichifukujin), and Jinushi-no-Ōkami. The shrine has a deep connection to {{ill|Minamoto no Yoritomo|ja|源頼朝}}, who revered it, and it features sacred trees planted by Yoritomo, including a dragon-shaped sacred ginkgo tree. [[Kainan Shrine]] is a regional [[Sōja (Shinto)|Sōja shrine]]. It enshrines many kami of the local region. It contrasts with provincial Soja shrines which enshrine all the kami of a provincehttps://archive.ph/wip/XtZfZ == Enshrined Deities == * '''Fujiwara Sukemitsu (藤原資盈)''' * '''Mitsuwatari-hime (盈渡姫)''' * '''Jinushi-no-Ōkami (地主大神)''' * '''Susanoo (素戔嗚尊)''' * '''{{ill|Otori-sama|ja|天日鷲神}} (天日鷲神)''' * '''Sugawara no Michizane (Sugawara no Michizane)''' * '''Senryū Benzaiten (筌龍弁財天)''' == History == During the reign of {{ill|Emperor Seiwa|ja|Emperor Seiwa}}, Fujiwara Sukemitsu was exiled due to a false accusation related to a succession dispute. In {{ill|Jōgan (era)|ja|貞観}} 6 (864 CE), Sukemitsu was shipwrecked on the {{ill|Miura Peninsula|ja|三浦半島}} while traveling to his post in {{ill|Tsukushi Province|ja|筑紫国}}. The locals revered Sukemitsu for his efforts in quelling pirates and improving welfare. After his death in Jōgan 8 (866 CE), a shrine was built to honor him. In {{ill|Tengen (era)|ja|天元}} 5 (982 CE), the current shrine building was established, and the shrine became the total guardian of {{ill|Miura District, Kanagawa|ja|三浦郡}}. Minamoto no Yoritomo, following his 1180 uprising, held the shrine in high regard. Legend states that Yoritomo planted a pair of sacred ginkgo trees as offerings in 1185. The shrine received the title of "Sōchinju" (総鎮守, General Guardian Shrine) of the Miura Peninsula in 1719 (Kyōhō 4). It was designated a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}} in 1873 (Meiji 6) and listed as a shrine for offering government-provided ritual offerings in 1907 (Meiji 40). The ritual {{ill|Chakkirako|ja|チャッキラコ}}, unique to the shrine, was inscribed as a UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage in 2009. The shrine's buildings were designated as Important Cultural Properties by Kanagawa Prefecture in 2011. In 2021, the shrine became the guardian of the "Animal Shichifukujin" statues from the defunct Keikyu Aburatsubo Marine Park. == Shrine Grounds == === Main Features === * '''Main Hall (本殿)''' - Built in [[Shimmei-zukuri]] style. * '''Worship Hall (拝殿)''' - [[Gongen-zukuri]] style. * '''Sacred Ginkgo Trees''' - Planted by Minamoto no Yoritomo, the female tree's drooping branches symbolize fertility and are touched by women seeking blessings for lactation and childbirth. The male tree resembles a dragon. Designated as a Natural Monument of Miura City. === Sub-Shrines === * '''Ryūjin and Suijin Shrines''' - Sacred to water and dragon deities. * '''Hōsō Shrine''' - Dedicated to Minamoto no Tametomo, protector against disease. * '''Kōya Shrine''' - Worships Iwaka Mutsukari no Mikoto, the deity of cuisine and cooking. * '''Mitama Shrine''' - Dedicated to Kamakura Goro Kagemasa, believed to heal eye diseases. * '''Fukutoku Inari Shrine''' - For prosperity and safety in trade and fishing. * '''Konpira Shrine''' - Dedicated to Ōmononushi, a deity of maritime safety and commerce. === Notable Festivals and Rituals === * '''New Year's Eve (January 1)''' - Saitan-sai with lion dances for exorcism. * '''January 15''' - {{ill|Chakkirako}}: A unique dance registered as a UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage. * '''Summer Festival''' - Two-day event with traditional mikoshi processions. * '''Menkagura (November)''' - A traditional masked dance representing local folklore and Shinto traditions. == Access == * From '''Keikyu Kurihama Line''': - Take a bus from Miura-Kaigan Station or Misaki-guchi Station to Misaki Port (三崎港), then walk 2 minutes north. * Parking available near the shrine office. == References == {{reflist}} == See Also == * {{ill|Power spots|ja|パワースポット}} * {{ill|Minamoto no Yoritomo|ja|源頼朝}} * {{ill|Ryūjin|ja|龍神}} [[Category:Shrines in Kanagawa Prefecture]] Two days before Marine Day in July |rituals = [[Chakkirako]] (UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage) }} '''Kainan Shrine''' (海南神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Miura, Kanagawa|ja|三浦市}}, {{ill|Kanagawa Prefecture|ja|神奈川県}}, slightly inland from {{ill|Misaki Fishing Port|ja|三崎漁港}}. It is the total guardian shrine of the {{ill|Miura Peninsula|ja|三浦半島}} in {{ill|Sagami Province|ja|相模国}}, enshrining Fujiwara Sukemitsu, Mitsuwatari-hime, Senryū Benzaiten (part of the Miura Shichifukujin), and Jinushi-no-Ōkami. The shrine has a deep connection to {{ill|Minamoto no Yoritomo|ja|源頼朝}}, who revered it, and it features sacred trees planted by Yoritomo, including a dragon-shaped sacred ginkgo tree. [[Kainan Shrine]] is a regional [[Sōja (Shinto)|Sōja shrine]]. It enshrines many kami of the local region. It contrasts with provincial Soja shrines which enshrine all the kami of a provincehttps://archive.ph/wip/XtZfZ == Enshrined Deities == * '''Fujiwara Sukemitsu (藤原資盈)''' * '''Mitsuwatari-hime (盈渡姫)''' * '''Jinushi-no-Ōkami (地主大神)''' * '''Susanoo (素戔嗚尊)''' * '''{{ill|Otori-sama|ja|天日鷲神}} (天日鷲神)''' * '''Sugawara no Michizane (Sugawara no Michizane)''' * '''Senryū Benzaiten (筌龍弁財天)''' == History == During the reign of {{ill|Emperor Seiwa|ja|Emperor Seiwa}}, Fujiwara Sukemitsu was exiled due to a false accusation related to a succession dispute. In {{ill|Jōgan (era)|ja|貞観}} 6 (864 CE), Sukemitsu was shipwrecked on the {{ill|Miura Peninsula|ja|三浦半島}} while traveling to his post in {{ill|Tsukushi Province|ja|筑紫国}}. The locals revered Sukemitsu for his efforts in quelling pirates and improving welfare. After his death in Jōgan 8 (866 CE), a shrine was built to honor him. In {{ill|Tengen (era)|ja|天元}} 5 (982 CE), the current shrine building was established, and the shrine became the total guardian of {{ill|Miura District, Kanagawa|ja|三浦郡}}. Minamoto no Yoritomo, following his 1180 uprising, held the shrine in high regard. Legend states that Yoritomo planted a pair of sacred ginkgo trees as offerings in 1185. The shrine received the title of "Sōchinju" (総鎮守, General Guardian Shrine) of the Miura Peninsula in 1719 (Kyōhō 4). It was designated a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}} in 1873 (Meiji 6) and listed as a shrine for offering government-provided ritual offerings in 1907 (Meiji 40). The ritual {{ill|Chakkirako|ja|チャッキラコ}}, unique to the shrine, was inscribed as a UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage in 2009. The shrine's buildings were designated as Important Cultural Properties by Kanagawa Prefecture in 2011. In 2021, the shrine became the guardian of the "Animal Shichifukujin" statues from the defunct Keikyu Aburatsubo Marine Park. == Shrine Grounds == === Main Features === * '''Main Hall (本殿)''' - Built in [[Shimmei-zukuri]] style. * '''Worship Hall (拝殿)''' - [[Gongen-zukuri]] style. * '''Sacred Ginkgo Trees''' - Planted by Minamoto no Yoritomo, the female tree's drooping branches symbolize fertility and are touched by women seeking blessings for lactation and childbirth. The male tree resembles a dragon. Designated as a Natural Monument of Miura City. === Sub-Shrines === * '''Ryūjin and Suijin Shrines''' - Sacred to water and dragon deities. * '''Hōsō Shrine''' - Dedicated to Minamoto no Tametomo, protector against disease. * '''Kōya Shrine''' - Worships Iwaka Mutsukari no Mikoto, the deity of cuisine and cooking. * '''Mitama Shrine''' - Dedicated to Kamakura Goro Kagemasa, believed to heal eye diseases. * '''Fukutoku Inari Shrine''' - For prosperity and safety in trade and fishing. * '''Konpira Shrine''' - Dedicated to Ōmononushi, a deity of maritime safety and commerce. === Notable Festivals and Rituals === * '''New Year's Eve (January 1)''' - Saitan-sai with lion dances for exorcism. * '''January 15''' - {{ill|Chakkirako}}: A unique dance registered as a UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage. * '''Summer Festival''' - Two-day event with traditional mikoshi processions. * '''Menkagura (November)''' - A traditional masked dance representing local folklore and Shinto traditions. == Access == * From '''Keikyu Kurihama Line''': - Take a bus from Miura-Kaigan Station or Misaki-guchi Station to Misaki Port (三崎港), then walk 2 minutes north. * Parking available near the shrine office. == References == {{reflist}} == See Also == * {{ill|Power spots|ja|パワースポット}} * {{ill|Minamoto no Yoritomo|ja|源頼朝}} * {{ill|Ryūjin|ja|龍神}} [[Category:Shrines in Kanagawa Prefecture]]
