Two days before Marine Day in July |rituals = [[:en:Chakkirako|Chakkirako]] (UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage) |location = {{ill|Miura|WD=Q823886}} |coordinates = {{Coord|35.14275555555555|N|139.61884444444445|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} }} '''Kainan Shrine''' (海南神社) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in [[:en:Miura, Kanagawa|Miura, Kanagawa]], [[:en:Kanagawa Prefecture|Kanagawa Prefecture]], slightly inland from {{ill|Misaki Fishing Port|ja|三崎漁港|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Misaki Fishing Port|1=Port of Misaki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q3316212}}. It is the total guardian shrine of the [[:en:Miura Peninsula|Miura Peninsula]] in [[:en:Sagami Province|Sagami Province]], enshrining Fujiwara Sukemitsu, Mitsuwatari-hime, Senryū Benzaiten (part of the Miura Shichifukujin), and Jinushi-no-Ōkami. The shrine has a deep connection to [[:en:Minamoto no Yoritomo|Minamoto no Yoritomo]], who revered it, and it features sacred trees planted by Yoritomo, including a dragon-shaped sacred ginkgo tree. [[Kainan Shrine]] is a regional [[Sōja shrine|Sōja shrine]]. It enshrines many kami of the local region. It contrasts with provincial Soja shrines which enshrine all the kami of a provincehttps://archive.ph/wip/XtZfZ == Enshrined Deities == * '''Fujiwara Sukemitsu (藤原資盈)''' * '''Mitsuwatari-hime (盈渡姫)''' * '''Jinushi-no-Ōkami (地主大神)''' * '''Susanoo (素戔嗚尊)''' * '''{{ill|Otori-sama|ja|天日鷲神|1=Otori-sama|lt=Otori-sama|2=ja|3=天日鷲神|4=zh|5=天日鷲神|6=ko|7=아메노히와시노카미|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Otori-sama|qq=}} (天日鷲神)''' * '''Sugawara no Michizane (Sugawara no Michizane)''' * '''Senryū Benzaiten (筌龍弁財天)''' == History == During the reign of {{ill|Emperor Seiwa|ja|Emperor Seiwa|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Emperor Seiwa|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|WD=Q135505731}}, Fujiwara Sukemitsu was exiled due to a false accusation related to a succession dispute. In [[:en:Zhenguan|Jōgan (era)]] 6 (864 CE), Sukemitsu was shipwrecked on the [[:en:Miura Peninsula|Miura Peninsula]] while traveling to his post in [[:en:Tsukushi Province|Tsukushi Province]]. The locals revered Sukemitsu for his efforts in quelling pirates and improving welfare. After his death in Jōgan 8 (866 CE), a shrine was built to honor him. In [[:en:Tengen|Tengen (era)]] 5 (982 CE), the current shrine building was established, and the shrine became the total guardian of [[:en:Miura District, Kanagawa|Miura District, Kanagawa]]. Minamoto no Yoritomo, following his 1180 uprising, held the shrine in high regard. Legend states that Yoritomo planted a pair of sacred ginkgo trees as offerings in 1185. The shrine received the title of "Sōchinju" (総鎮守, General Guardian Shrine) of the Miura Peninsula in 1719 (Kyōhō 4). It was designated a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gōsha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}} in 1873 (Meiji 6) and listed as a shrine for offering government-provided ritual offerings in 1907 (Meiji 40). The ritual [[:en:Chakkirako|Chakkirako]], unique to the shrine, was inscribed as a UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage in 2009. The shrine's buildings were designated as Important Cultural Properties by Kanagawa Prefecture in 2011. In 2021, the shrine became the guardian of the "Animal Shichifukujin" statues from the defunct Keikyu Aburatsubo Marine Park. == Shrine Grounds == === Main Features === * '''Main Hall (本殿)''' - Built in [[Shimmei-zukuri]] style. * '''Worship Hall (拝殿)''' - [[Ishi-no-ma-zukuri|Gongen-zukuri]] style. * '''Sacred Ginkgo Trees''' - Planted by Minamoto no Yoritomo, the female tree's drooping branches symbolize fertility and are touched by women seeking blessings for lactation and childbirth. The male tree resembles a dragon. Designated as a Natural Monument of Miura City. === Sub-Shrines === * '''Ryūjin and Suijin Shrines''' - Sacred to water and dragon deities. * '''Hōsō Shrine''' - Dedicated to Minamoto no Tametomo, protector against disease. * '''Kōya Shrine''' - Worships Iwaka Mutsukari no Mikoto, the deity of cuisine and cooking. * '''Mitama Shrine''' - Dedicated to Kamakura Goro Kagemasa, believed to heal eye diseases. * '''Fukutoku Inari Shrine''' - For prosperity and safety in trade and fishing. * '''Konpira Shrine''' - Dedicated to Ōmononushi, a deity of maritime safety and commerce. === Notable Festivals and Rituals === * '''New Year's Eve (January 1)''' - Saitan-sai with lion dances for exorcism. * '''January 15''' - {{ill|Chakkirako|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chakkirako|qq=}}: A unique dance registered as a UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage. * '''Summer Festival''' - Two-day event with traditional mikoshi processions. * '''Menkagura (November)''' - A traditional masked dance representing local folklore and Shinto traditions. == Access == * From '''Keikyu Kurihama Line''': ** Take a bus from Miura-Kaigan Station or Misaki-guchi Station to Misaki Port (三崎港), then walk 2 minutes north. * Parking available near the shrine office. == References == {{reflist}} == See Also == * [[:en:Power spot (spirituality)|Power spots]] * [[:en:Minamoto no Yoritomo|Minamoto no Two days before Marine Day in July |rituals = [[:en:Chakkirako|Chakkirako]] (UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage) |location = {{ill|Miura|WD=Q823886}} |coordinates = {{Coord|35.14275555555555|N|139.61884444444445|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} }} '''Kainan Shrine''' (海南神社) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in [[:en:Miura, Kanagawa|Miura, Kanagawa]], [[:en:Kanagawa Prefecture|Kanagawa Prefecture]], slightly inland from {{ill|Misaki Fishing Port|ja|三崎漁港|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Misaki Fishing Port|1=Port of Misaki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q3316212}}. It is the total guardian shrine of the [[:en:Miura Peninsula|Miura Peninsula]] in [[:en:Sagami Province|Sagami Province]], enshrining Fujiwara Sukemitsu, Mitsuwatari-hime, Senryū Benzaiten (part of the Miura Shichifukujin), and Jinushi-no-Ōkami. The shrine has a deep connection to [[:en:Minamoto no Yoritomo|Minamoto no Yoritomo]], who revered it, and it features sacred trees planted by Yoritomo, including a dragon-shaped sacred ginkgo tree. [[Kainan Shrine]] is a regional [[Sōja shrine|Sōja shrine]]. It enshrines many kami of the local region. It contrasts with provincial Soja shrines which enshrine all the kami of a provincehttps://archive.ph/wip/XtZfZ == Enshrined Deities == * '''Fujiwara Sukemitsu (藤原資盈)''' * '''Mitsuwatari-hime (盈渡姫)''' * '''Jinushi-no-Ōkami (地主大神)''' * '''Susanoo (素戔嗚尊)''' * '''{{ill|Otori-sama|ja|天日鷲神|1=Otori-sama|lt=Otori-sama|2=ja|3=天日鷲神|4=zh|5=天日鷲神|6=ko|7=아메노히와시노카미|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Otori-sama|qq=}} (天日鷲神)''' * '''Sugawara no Michizane (Sugawara no Michizane)''' * '''Senryū Benzaiten (筌龍弁財天)''' == History == During the reign of {{ill|Emperor Seiwa|ja|Emperor Seiwa|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Emperor Seiwa|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|WD=Q135505731}}, Fujiwara Sukemitsu was exiled due to a false accusation related to a succession dispute. In [[:en:Zhenguan|Jōgan (era)]] 6 (864 CE), Sukemitsu was shipwrecked on the [[:en:Miura Peninsula|Miura Peninsula]] while traveling to his post in [[:en:Tsukushi Province|Tsukushi Province]]. The locals revered Sukemitsu for his efforts in quelling pirates and improving welfare. After his death in Jōgan 8 (866 CE), a shrine was built to honor him. In [[:en:Tengen|Tengen (era)]] 5 (982 CE), the current shrine building was established, and the shrine became the total guardian of [[:en:Miura District, Kanagawa|Miura District, Kanagawa]]. Minamoto no Yoritomo, following his 1180 uprising, held the shrine in high regard. Legend states that Yoritomo planted a pair of sacred ginkgo trees as offerings in 1185. The shrine received the title of "Sōchinju" (総鎮守, General Guardian Shrine) of the Miura Peninsula in 1719 (Kyōhō 4). It was designated a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gōsha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}} in 1873 (Meiji 6) and listed as a shrine for offering government-provided ritual offerings in 1907 (Meiji 40). The ritual [[:en:Chakkirako|Chakkirako]], unique to the shrine, was inscribed as a UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage in 2009. The shrine's buildings were designated as Important Cultural Properties by Kanagawa Prefecture in 2011. In 2021, the shrine became the guardian of the "Animal Shichifukujin" statues from the defunct Keikyu Aburatsubo Marine Park. == Shrine Grounds == === Main Features === * '''Main Hall (本殿)''' - Built in [[Shimmei-zukuri]] style. * '''Worship Hall (拝殿)''' - [[Ishi-no-ma-zukuri|Gongen-zukuri]] style. * '''Sacred Ginkgo Trees''' - Planted by Minamoto no Yoritomo, the female tree's drooping branches symbolize fertility and are touched by women seeking blessings for lactation and childbirth. The male tree resembles a dragon. Designated as a Natural Monument of Miura City. === Sub-Shrines === * '''Ryūjin and Suijin Shrines''' - Sacred to water and dragon deities. * '''Hōsō Shrine''' - Dedicated to Minamoto no Tametomo, protector against disease. * '''Kōya Shrine''' - Worships Iwaka Mutsukari no Mikoto, the deity of cuisine and cooking. * '''Mitama Shrine''' - Dedicated to Kamakura Goro Kagemasa, believed to heal eye diseases. * '''Fukutoku Inari Shrine''' - For prosperity and safety in trade and fishing. * '''Konpira Shrine''' - Dedicated to Ōmononushi, a deity of maritime safety and commerce. === Notable Festivals and Rituals === * '''New Year's Eve (January 1)''' - Saitan-sai with lion dances for exorcism. * '''January 15''' - {{ill|Chakkirako|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chakkirako|qq=}}: A unique dance registered as a UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage. * '''Summer Festival''' - Two-day event with traditional mikoshi processions. * '''Menkagura (November)''' - A traditional masked dance representing local folklore and Shinto traditions. == Access == * From '''Keikyu Kurihama Line''': ** Take a bus from Miura-Kaigan Station or Misaki-guchi Station to Misaki Port (三崎港), then walk 2 minutes north. * Parking available near the shrine office. == References == {{reflist}} == See Also == * [[:en:Power spot (spirituality)|Power spots]] * [[:en:Minamoto no Yoritomo|Minamoto no Two days before Marine Day in July |rituals = [[:en:Chakkirako|Chakkirako]] (UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage) |location = {{ill|Miura|WD=Q823886}} |coordinates = {{Coord|35.14275555555555|N|139.61884444444445|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} }} '''Kainan Shrine''' (海南神社) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in [[:en:Miura, Kanagawa|Miura, Kanagawa]], [[:en:Kanagawa Prefecture|Kanagawa Prefecture]], slightly inland from {{ill|Misaki Fishing Port|ja|三崎漁港|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Misaki Fishing Port|1=Port of Misaki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q3316212}}. It is the total guardian shrine of the [[:en:Miura Peninsula|Miura Peninsula]] in [[:en:Sagami Province|Sagami Province]], enshrining Fujiwara Sukemitsu, Mitsuwatari-hime, Senryū Benzaiten (part of the Miura Shichifukujin), and Jinushi-no-Ōkami. The shrine has a deep connection to [[:en:Minamoto no Yoritomo|Minamoto no Yoritomo]], who revered it, and it features sacred trees planted by Yoritomo, including a dragon-shaped sacred ginkgo tree. [[Kainan Shrine]] is a regional [[Sōja shrine|Sōja shrine]]. It enshrines many kami of the local region. It contrasts with provincial Soja shrines which enshrine all the kami of a provincehttps://archive.ph/wip/XtZfZ == Enshrined Deities == * '''Fujiwara Sukemitsu (藤原資盈)''' * '''Mitsuwatari-hime (盈渡姫)''' * '''Jinushi-no-Ōkami (地主大神)''' * '''Susanoo (素戔嗚尊)''' * '''{{ill|Otori-sama|ja|天日鷲神|1=Otori-sama|lt=Otori-sama|2=ja|3=天日鷲神|4=zh|5=天日鷲神|6=ko|7=아메노히와시노카미|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Otori-sama|qq=}} (天日鷲神)''' * '''Sugawara no Michizane (Sugawara no Michizane)''' * '''Senryū Benzaiten (筌龍弁財天)''' == History == During the reign of {{ill|Emperor Seiwa|ja|Emperor Seiwa|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Emperor Seiwa|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|WD=Q135505731}}, Fujiwara Sukemitsu was exiled due to a false accusation related to a succession dispute. In [[:en:Zhenguan|Jōgan (era)]] 6 (864 CE), Sukemitsu was shipwrecked on the [[:en:Miura Peninsula|Miura Peninsula]] while traveling to his post in [[:en:Tsukushi Province|Tsukushi Province]]. The locals revered Sukemitsu for his efforts in quelling pirates and improving welfare. After his death in Jōgan 8 (866 CE), a shrine was built to honor him. In [[:en:Tengen|Tengen (era)]] 5 (982 CE), the current shrine building was established, and the shrine became the total guardian of [[:en:Miura District, Kanagawa|Miura District, Kanagawa]]. Minamoto no Yoritomo, following his 1180 uprising, held the shrine in high regard. Legend states that Yoritomo planted a pair of sacred ginkgo trees as offerings in 1185. The shrine received the title of "Sōchinju" (総鎮守, General Guardian Shrine) of the Miura Peninsula in 1719 (Kyōhō 4). It was designated a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gōsha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}} in 1873 (Meiji 6) and listed as a shrine for offering government-provided ritual offerings in 1907 (Meiji 40). The ritual [[:en:Chakkirako|Chakkirako]], unique to the shrine, was inscribed as a UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage in 2009. The shrine's buildings were designated as Important Cultural Properties by Kanagawa Prefecture in 2011. In 2021, the shrine became the guardian of the "Animal Shichifukujin" statues from the defunct Keikyu Aburatsubo Marine Park. == Shrine Grounds == === Main Features === * '''Main Hall (本殿)''' - Built in [[Shimmei-zukuri]] style. * '''Worship Hall (拝殿)''' - [[Ishi-no-ma-zukuri|Gongen-zukuri]] style. * '''Sacred Ginkgo Trees''' - Planted by Minamoto no Yoritomo, the female tree's drooping branches symbolize fertility and are touched by women seeking blessings for lactation and childbirth. The male tree resembles a dragon. Designated as a Natural Monument of Miura City. === Sub-Shrines === * '''Ryūjin and Suijin Shrines''' - Sacred to water and dragon deities. * '''Hōsō Shrine''' - Dedicated to Minamoto no Tametomo, protector against disease. * '''Kōya Shrine''' - Worships Iwaka Mutsukari no Mikoto, the deity of cuisine and cooking. * '''Mitama Shrine''' - Dedicated to Kamakura Goro Kagemasa, believed to heal eye diseases. * '''Fukutoku Inari Shrine''' - For prosperity and safety in trade and fishing. * '''Konpira Shrine''' - Dedicated to Ōmononushi, a deity of maritime safety and commerce. === Notable Festivals and Rituals === * '''New Year's Eve (January 1)''' - Saitan-sai with lion dances for exorcism. * '''January 15''' - {{ill|Chakkirako|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chakkirako|qq=}}: A unique dance registered as a UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage. * '''Summer Festival''' - Two-day event with traditional mikoshi processions. * '''Menkagura (November)''' - A traditional masked dance representing local folklore and Shinto traditions. == Access == * From '''Keikyu Kurihama Line''': ** Take a bus from Miura-Kaigan Station or Misaki-guchi Station to Misaki Port (三崎港), then walk 2 minutes north. * Parking available near the shrine office. == References == {{reflist}} == See Also == * [[:en:Power spot (spirituality)|Power spots]] * [[:en:Minamoto no Yoritomo|Minamoto no Two days before Marine Day in July |rituals = [[:en:Chakkirako|Chakkirako]] (UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage) |location = {{ill|Miura|WD=Q823886}} |coordinates = {{Coord|35.14275555555555|N|139.61884444444445|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} }} '''Kainan Shrine''' (海南神社) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in [[:en:Miura, Kanagawa|Miura, Kanagawa]], [[:en:Kanagawa Prefecture|Kanagawa Prefecture]], slightly inland from {{ill|Misaki Fishing Port|ja|三崎漁港|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Misaki Fishing Port|1=Port of Misaki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q3316212}}. It is the total guardian shrine of the [[:en:Miura Peninsula|Miura Peninsula]] in [[:en:Sagami Province|Sagami Province]], enshrining Fujiwara Sukemitsu, Mitsuwatari-hime, Senryū Benzaiten (part of the Miura Shichifukujin), and Jinushi-no-Ōkami. The shrine has a deep connection to [[:en:Minamoto no Yoritomo|Minamoto no Yoritomo]], who revered it, and it features sacred trees planted by Yoritomo, including a dragon-shaped sacred ginkgo tree. [[Kainan Shrine]] is a regional [[Sōja shrine|Sōja shrine]]. It enshrines many kami of the local region. It contrasts with provincial Soja shrines which enshrine all the kami of a provincehttps://archive.ph/wip/XtZfZ == Enshrined Deities == * '''Fujiwara Sukemitsu (藤原資盈)''' * '''Mitsuwatari-hime (盈渡姫)''' * '''Jinushi-no-Ōkami (地主大神)''' * '''Susanoo (素戔嗚尊)''' * '''{{ill|Otori-sama|ja|天日鷲神|1=Otori-sama|lt=Otori-sama|2=ja|3=天日鷲神|4=zh|5=天日鷲神|6=ko|7=아메노히와시노카미|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Otori-sama|qq=}} (天日鷲神)''' * '''Sugawara no Michizane (Sugawara no Michizane)''' * '''Senryū Benzaiten (筌龍弁財天)''' == History == During the reign of {{ill|Emperor Seiwa|ja|Emperor Seiwa|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Emperor Seiwa|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|WD=Q135505731}}, Fujiwara Sukemitsu was exiled due to a false accusation related to a succession dispute. In [[:en:Zhenguan|Jōgan (era)]] 6 (864 CE), Sukemitsu was shipwrecked on the [[:en:Miura Peninsula|Miura Peninsula]] while traveling to his post in [[:en:Tsukushi Province|Tsukushi Province]]. The locals revered Sukemitsu for his efforts in quelling pirates and improving welfare. After his death in Jōgan 8 (866 CE), a shrine was built to honor him. In [[:en:Tengen|Tengen (era)]] 5 (982 CE), the current shrine building was established, and the shrine became the total guardian of [[:en:Miura District, Kanagawa|Miura District, Kanagawa]]. Minamoto no Yoritomo, following his 1180 uprising, held the shrine in high regard. Legend states that Yoritomo planted a pair of sacred ginkgo trees as offerings in 1185. The shrine received the title of "Sōchinju" (総鎮守, General Guardian Shrine) of the Miura Peninsula in 1719 (Kyōhō 4). It was designated a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gōsha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}} in 1873 (Meiji 6) and listed as a shrine for offering government-provided ritual offerings in 1907 (Meiji 40). The ritual [[:en:Chakkirako|Chakkirako]], unique to the shrine, was inscribed as a UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage in 2009. The shrine's buildings were designated as Important Cultural Properties by Kanagawa Prefecture in 2011. In 2021, the shrine became the guardian of the "Animal Shichifukujin" statues from the defunct Keikyu Aburatsubo Marine Park. == Shrine Grounds == === Main Features === * '''Main Hall (本殿)''' - Built in [[Shimmei-zukuri]] style. * '''Worship Hall (拝殿)''' - [[Ishi-no-ma-zukuri|Gongen-zukuri]] style. * '''Sacred Ginkgo Trees''' - Planted by Minamoto no Yoritomo, the female tree's drooping branches symbolize fertility and are touched by women seeking blessings for lactation and childbirth. The male tree resembles a dragon. Two days before Marine Day in July |rituals = [[:en:Chakkirako|Chakkirako]] (UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage) |location = {{ill|Miura|WD=Q823886}} |coordinates = {{Coord|35.14275555555555|N|139.61884444444445|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} }} '''Kainan Shrine''' (海南神社) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in [[:en:Miura, Kanagawa|Miura, Kanagawa]], [[:en:Kanagawa Prefecture|Kanagawa Prefecture]], slightly inland from {{ill|Misaki Fishing Port|ja|三崎漁港|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Misaki Fishing Port|1=Port of Misaki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q3316212}}. It is the total guardian shrine of the [[:en:Miura Peninsula|Miura Peninsula]] in [[:en:Sagami Province|Sagami Province]], enshrining Fujiwara Sukemitsu, Mitsuwatari-hime, Senryū Benzaiten (part of the Miura Shichifukujin), and Jinushi-no-Ōkami. The shrine has a deep connection to [[:en:Minamoto no Yoritomo|Minamoto no Yoritomo]], who revered it, and it features sacred trees planted by Yoritomo, including a dragon-shaped sacred ginkgo tree. [[Kainan Shrine]] is a regional [[Sōja shrine|Sōja shrine]]. It enshrines many kami of the local region. It contrasts with provincial Soja shrines which enshrine all the kami of a provincehttps://archive.ph/wip/XtZfZ == Enshrined Deities == * '''Fujiwara Sukemitsu (藤原資盈)''' * '''Mitsuwatari-hime (盈渡姫)''' * '''Jinushi-no-Ōkami (地主大神)''' * '''Susanoo (素戔嗚尊)''' * '''{{ill|Otori-sama|ja|天日鷲神|1=Otori-sama|lt=Otori-sama|2=ja|3=天日鷲神|4=zh|5=天日鷲神|6=ko|7=아메노히와시노카미|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Otori-sama|qq=}} (天日鷲神)''' * '''Sugawara no Michizane (Sugawara no Michizane)''' * '''Senryū Benzaiten (筌龍弁財天)''' == History == During the reign of {{ill|Emperor Seiwa|ja|Emperor Seiwa|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Emperor Seiwa|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|WD=Q135505731}}, Fujiwara Sukemitsu was exiled due to a false accusation related to a succession dispute. In [[:en:Zhenguan|Jōgan (era)]] 6 (864 CE), Sukemitsu was shipwrecked on the [[:en:Miura Peninsula|Miura Peninsula]] while traveling to his post in [[:en:Tsukushi Province|Tsukushi Province]]. The locals revered Sukemitsu for his efforts in quelling pirates and improving welfare. After his death in Jōgan 8 (866 CE), a shrine was built to honor him. In [[:en:Tengen|Tengen (era)]] 5 (982 CE), the current shrine building was established, and the shrine became the total guardian of [[:en:Miura District, Kanagawa|Miura District, Kanagawa]]. Minamoto no Yoritomo, following his 1180 uprising, held the shrine in high regard. Legend states that Yoritomo planted a pair of sacred ginkgo trees as offerings in 1185. The locals revered Sukemitsu for his efforts in quelling pirates and improving welfare. After his death in Jōgan 8 (866 CE), a shrine was built to honor him. In [[:en:Tengen|Tengen (era)]] 5 (982 CE), the current shrine building was established, and the shrine became the total guardian of [[:en:Miura District, Kanagawa|Miura District, Kanagawa]]. Minamoto no Yoritomo, following his 1180 uprising, held the shrine in high regard. Legend states that Yoritomo planted a pair of sacred ginkgo trees as offerings in 1185. The shrine received the title of "Sōchinju" (総鎮守, General Guardian Shrine) of the Miura Peninsula in 1719 (Kyōhō 4). It was designated a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gōsha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}} in 1873 (Meiji 6) and listed as a shrine for offering government-provided ritual offerings in 1907 (Meiji 40). The ritual [[:en:Chakkirako|Chakkirako]], unique to the shrine, was inscribed as a UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage in 2009. The shrine's buildings were designated as Important Cultural Properties by Kanagawa Prefecture in 2011. In 2021, the shrine became the guardian of the "Animal Shichifukujin" statues from the defunct Keikyu Aburatsubo Marine Park. == Shrine Grounds == === Main Features === * '''Main Hall (本殿)''' - Built in [[Shimmei-zukuri]] style. * '''Worship Hall (拝殿)''' - [[Ishi-no-ma-zukuri|Gongen-zukuri]] style. * '''Sacred Ginkgo Trees''' - Planted by Minamoto no Yoritomo, the female tree's drooping branches symbolize fertility and are touched by women seeking blessings for lactation and childbirth. The male tree resembles a dragon. Designated as a Natural Monument of Miura City. === Sub-Shrines === * '''Ryūjin and Suijin Shrines''' - Sacred to water and dragon deities. * '''Hōsō Shrine''' - Dedicated to Minamoto no Tametomo, protector against disease. * '''Kōya Shrine''' - Worships Iwaka Mutsukari no Mikoto, the deity of cuisine and cooking. * '''Mitama Shrine''' - Dedicated to Kamakura Goro Kagemasa, believed to heal eye diseases. * '''Fukutoku Inari Shrine''' - For prosperity and safety in trade and fishing. * '''Konpira Shrine''' - Dedicated to Ōmononushi, a deity of maritime safety and commerce. === Notable Festivals and Rituals === * '''New Year's Eve (January 1)''' - Saitan-sai with lion dances for exorcism. * '''January 15''' - {{ill|Chakkirako|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chakkirako|qq=}}: A unique dance registered as a UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage. * '''Summer Festival''' - Two-day event with traditional mikoshi processions. * '''Menkagura (November)''' - A traditional masked dance representing local folklore and Shinto traditions. == Access == * From '''Keikyu Kurihama Line''': ** Take a bus from Miura-Kaigan Station or Misaki-guchi Station to Misaki Port (三崎港), then walk 2 Two days before Marine Day in July |rituals = {{ill|Chakkirako|en|Chakkirako|WD=Q11318123|lt=Chakkirako}} (UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage) |location = {{ill|Miura|WD=Q823886}} |coordinates = {{Coord|35.14275555555555|N|139.61884444444445|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} }} '''Kainan Shrine''' (海南神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} located in {{ill|Miura, Kanagawa|en|Miura, Kanagawa|WD=Q823886|lt=Miura, Kanagawa}}, {{ill|Kanagawa Prefecture|en|Kanagawa Prefecture|WD=Q127513|lt=Kanagawa Prefecture}}, slightly inland from {{ill|Misaki Fishing Port|ja|三崎漁港|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Misaki Fishing Port|1=Port of Misaki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q3316212}}. It is the total guardian shrine of the {{ill|Miura Peninsula|en|Miura Peninsula|WD=Q536757|lt=Miura Peninsula}} in {{ill|Sagami Province|en|Sagami Province|WD=Q1053732|lt=Sagami Province}}, enshrining Fujiwara Sukemitsu, Mitsuwatari-hime, Senryū Benzaiten (part of the Miura Shichifukujin), and Jinushi-no-Ōkami. The shrine has a deep connection to {{ill|Minamoto no Yoritomo|en|Minamoto no Yoritomo|WD=Q242800|lt=Minamoto no Yoritomo}}, who revered it, and it features sacred trees planted by Yoritomo, including a dragon-shaped sacred ginkgo tree. [[Kainan Shrine]] is a regional [[Sōja shrine|Sōja shrine]]. It enshrines many kami of the local region. It contrasts with provincial Soja shrines which enshrine all the kami of a provincehttps://archive.ph/wip/XtZfZ == Enshrined Deities == * '''Fujiwara Sukemitsu (藤原資盈)''' * '''Mitsuwatari-hime (盈渡姫)''' * '''Jinushi-no-Ōkami (地主大神)''' * '''Susanoo (素戔嗚尊)''' * '''{{ill|Otori-sama|ja|天日鷲神|1=Otori-sama|lt=Otori-sama|2=ja|3=天日鷲神|4=zh|5=天日鷲神|6=ko|7=아메노히와시노카미|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Otori-sama|qq=}} (天日鷲神)''' * '''Sugawara no Michizane (Sugawara no Michizane)''' * '''Senryū Benzaiten (筌龍弁財天)''' == History == During the reign of {{ill|Emperor Seiwa|ja|Emperor Seiwa|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Emperor Seiwa|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|WD=Q135505731}}, Fujiwara Sukemitsu was exiled due to a false accusation related to a succession dispute. In {{ill|Zhenguan|en|Zhenguan|WD=Q3577278|lt=Jōgan (era)}} 6 (864 CE), Sukemitsu was shipwrecked on the {{ill|Miura Peninsula|en|Miura Peninsula|WD=Q536757|lt=Miura Peninsula}} while traveling to his post in {{ill|Tsukushi Province|en|Tsukushi Province|WD=Q1206461|lt=Tsukushi Province}}. The locals revered Sukemitsu for his efforts in quelling pirates and improving welfare. After his death in Jōgan 8 (866 CE), a shrine was built to honor him. In {{ill|Tengen|en|Tengen|WD=Q1185206|lt=Tengen (era)}} 5 (982 CE), the current shrine building was established, and the shrine became the total guardian of {{ill|Miura District, Kanagawa|en|Miura District, Kanagawa|WD=Q1203937|lt=Miura District, Kanagawa}}. Minamoto no Yoritomo, following his 1180 uprising, held the shrine in high regard. Legend states that Yoritomo planted a pair of sacred ginkgo trees as offerings in 1185. The shrine received the title of "Sōchinju" (総鎮守, General Guardian Shrine) of the Miura Peninsula in 1719 (Kyōhō 4). It was designated a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gōsha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}} in 1873 (Meiji 6) and listed as a shrine for offering government-provided ritual offerings in 1907 (Meiji 40). The ritual {{ill|Chakkirako|en|Chakkirako|WD=Q11318123|lt=Chakkirako}}, unique to the shrine, was inscribed as a UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage in 2009. The shrine's buildings were designated as Important Cultural Properties by Kanagawa Prefecture in 2011. In 2021, the shrine became the guardian of the "Animal Shichifukujin" statues from the defunct Keikyu Aburatsubo Marine Park. == Shrine Grounds == === Main Features === * '''Main Hall (本殿)''' - Built in [[Shimmei-zukuri]] style. * '''Worship Hall (拝殿)''' - [[Ishi-no-ma-zukuri|Gongen-zukuri]] style. * '''Sacred Ginkgo Trees''' - Planted by Minamoto no Yoritomo, the female tree's drooping branches symbolize fertility and are touched by women seeking blessings for lactation and childbirth. The male tree resembles a dragon. Designated as a Natural Monument of Miura City. === Sub-Shrines === * '''Ryūjin and Suijin Shrines''' - Sacred to water and dragon deities. * '''Hōsō Shrine''' - Dedicated to Minamoto no Tametomo, protector against disease. * '''Kōya Shrine''' - Worships Iwaka Mutsukari no Mikoto, the deity of cuisine and cooking. * '''Mitama Shrine''' - Dedicated to Kamakura Goro Kagemasa, believed to heal eye diseases. * '''Fukutoku Inari Shrine''' - For prosperity and safety in trade and fishing. * '''Konpira Shrine''' - Dedicated to Ōmononushi, a deity of maritime safety and commerce. === Notable Festivals and Rituals === * '''New Year's Eve (January 1)''' - Saitan-sai with lion dances for exorcism. * '''January 15''' - {{ill|Chakkirako|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chakkirako|qq=}}: A unique dance registered as a UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage. * '''Summer Festival''' - Two-day event with traditional mikoshi processions. * '''Menkagura (November)''' - A traditional masked dance representing local folklore and Shinto traditions. == Access == * From '''Keikyu Kurihama Line''': ** Take a bus from Miura-Kaigan Station or Misaki-guchi Station to Misaki Port (三崎港), then walk 2 minutes north. * Parking available near the shrine office. == References == {{reflist}} == See Also == * {{ill|Power spot (spirituality)|en|Power spot (spirituality)|WD=Q11329568|lt=Power spots}} * It is the total guardian shrine of the {{ill|Miura Peninsula|en|Miura Peninsula|WD=Q536757|lt=Miura Peninsula}} in {{ill|Sagami Province|en|Sagami Province|WD=Q1053732|lt=Sagami Province}}, enshrining Fujiwara Sukemitsu, Mitsuwatari-hime, Senryū Benzaiten (part of the Miura Shichifukujin), and Jinushi-no-Ōkami. The shrine has a deep connection to {{ill|Minamoto no Yoritomo|en|Minamoto no Yoritomo|WD=Q242800|lt=Minamoto no Yoritomo}}, who revered it, and it features sacred trees planted by Yoritomo, including a dragon-shaped sacred ginkgo tree. [[Kainan Shrine]] is a regional [[Sōja shrine|Sōja shrine]]. It enshrines many kami of the local region. It contrasts with provincial Soja shrines which enshrine all the kami of a provincehttps://archive.ph/wip/XtZfZ == Enshrined Deities == * '''Fujiwara Sukemitsu (藤原資盈)''' * '''Mitsuwatari-hime (盈渡姫)''' * '''Jinushi-no-Ōkami (地主大神)''' * '''Susanoo (素戔嗚尊)''' * '''{{ill|Otori-sama|ja|天日鷲神|1=Otori-sama|lt=Otori-sama|2=ja|3=天日鷲神|4=zh|5=天日鷲神|6=ko|7=아메노히와시노카미|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Otori-sama|qq=}} (天日鷲神)''' * '''Sugawara no Michizane (Sugawara no Michizane)''' * '''Senryū Benzaiten (筌龍弁財天)''' == History == During the reign of {{ill|Emperor Seiwa|ja|Emperor Seiwa|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Emperor Seiwa|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|WD=Q135505731}}, Fujiwara Sukemitsu was exiled due to a false accusation related to a succession dispute. In {{ill|Zhenguan|en|Zhenguan|WD=Q3577278|lt=Jōgan (era)}} 6 (864 CE), Sukemitsu was shipwrecked on the {{ill|Miura Peninsula|en|Miura Peninsula|WD=Q536757|lt=Miura Peninsula}} while traveling to his post in {{ill|Tsukushi Province|en|Tsukushi Province|WD=Q1206461|lt=Tsukushi Province}}. The locals revered Sukemitsu for his efforts in quelling pirates and improving welfare. After his death in Jōgan 8 (866 CE), a shrine was built to honor him. In {{ill|Tengen|en|Tengen|WD=Q1185206|lt=Tengen (era)}} 5 (982 CE), the current shrine building was established, and the shrine became the total guardian of {{ill|Miura District, Kanagawa|en|Miura District, Kanagawa|WD=Q1203937|lt=Miura District, Kanagawa}}. Minamoto no Yoritomo, following his 1180 uprising, held the shrine in high regard. Legend states that Yoritomo planted a pair of sacred ginkgo trees as offerings in 1185. The shrine received the title of "Sōchinju" (総鎮守, General Guardian Shrine) of the Miura Peninsula in 1719 (Kyōhō 4). It was designated a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gōsha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}} in 1873 (Meiji 6) and listed as a shrine for offering government-provided ritual offerings in 1907 (Meiji 40). The ritual {{ill|Chakkirako|en|Chakkirako|WD=Q11318123|lt=Chakkirako}}, unique to the shrine, was inscribed as a UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage in 2009. The shrine's buildings were designated as Important Cultural Properties by Kanagawa Prefecture in 2011. In 2021, the shrine became the guardian of the "Animal Shichifukujin" statues from the defunct Keikyu Aburatsubo Marine Park. == Shrine Grounds == === Main Features === * '''Main Hall (本殿)''' - Built in [[Shimmei-zukuri]] style. * '''Worship Hall (拝殿)''' - [[Ishi-no-ma-zukuri|Gongen-zukuri]] style. * '''Sacred Ginkgo Trees''' - Planted by Minamoto no Yoritomo, the female tree's drooping branches symbolize fertility and are touched by women seeking blessings for lactation and childbirth. The male tree resembles a dragon. Designated as a Natural Monument of Miura City. === Sub-Shrines === * '''Ryūjin and Suijin Shrines''' - Sacred to water and dragon deities. * '''Hōsō Shrine''' - Dedicated to Minamoto no Tametomo, protector against disease. * '''Kōya Shrine''' - Worships Iwaka Mutsukari no Mikoto, the deity of cuisine and cooking. * '''Mitama Shrine''' - Dedicated to Kamakura Goro Kagemasa, believed to heal eye diseases. * '''Fukutoku Inari Shrine''' - For prosperity and safety in trade and fishing. * '''Konpira Shrine''' - Dedicated to Ōmononushi, a deity of maritime safety and commerce. === Notable Festivals and Rituals === * '''New Year's Eve (January 1)''' - Saitan-sai with lion dances for exorcism. * '''January 15''' - {{ill|Chakkirako|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chakkirako|qq=}}: A unique dance registered as a UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage. * '''Summer Festival''' - Two-day event with traditional mikoshi processions. * '''Menkagura (November)''' - A traditional masked dance representing local folklore and Shinto traditions. == Access == * From '''Keikyu Kurihama Line''': ** Take a bus from Miura-Kaigan Station or Misaki-guchi Station to Misaki Port (三崎港), then walk 2 minutes north. * Parking available near the shrine office. == References == {{reflist}} == See Also == * {{ill|Power spot (spirituality)|en|Power spot (spirituality)|WD=Q11329568|lt=Power spots}} * Two days before Marine Day in July |rituals = {{ill|Chakkirako|en|Chakkirako|WD=Q11318123|lt=Chakkirako}} (UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage) |location = {{ill|Miura|WD=Q823886}} |coordinates = {{Coord|35.14275555555555|N|139.61884444444445|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} }} '''Kainan Shrine''' (海南神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} located in {{ill|Miura, Kanagawa|en|Miura, Kanagawa|WD=Q823886|lt=Miura, Kanagawa}}, {{ill|Kanagawa Prefecture|en|Kanagawa Prefecture|WD=Q127513|lt=Kanagawa Prefecture}}, slightly inland from {{ill|Misaki Fishing Port|ja|三崎漁港|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Misaki Fishing Port|1=Port of Misaki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q3316212}}. It is the total guardian shrine of the {{ill|Miura Peninsula|en|Miura Peninsula|WD=Q536757|lt=Miura Peninsula}} in {{ill|Sagami Province|en|Sagami Province|WD=Q1053732|lt=Sagami Province}}, enshrining Fujiwara Sukemitsu, Mitsuwatari-hime, Senryū Benzaiten (part of the Miura Shichifukujin), and Jinushi-no-Ōkami. The shrine has a deep connection to {{ill|Minamoto no Yoritomo|en|Minamoto no Yoritomo|WD=Q242800|lt=Minamoto no Yoritomo}}, who revered it, and it features sacred trees planted by Yoritomo, including a dragon-shaped sacred ginkgo tree. [[Kainan Shrine]] is a regional [[Sōja shrine|Sōja shrine]]. It enshrines many kami of the local region. It contrasts with provincial Soja shrines which enshrine all the kami of a provincehttps://archive.ph/wip/XtZfZ == Enshrined Deities == * '''Fujiwara Sukemitsu (藤原資盈)''' * '''Mitsuwatari-hime (盈渡姫)''' * '''Jinushi-no-Ōkami (地主大神)''' * '''Susanoo (素戔嗚尊)''' * '''{{ill|Otori-sama|ja|天日鷲神|1=Otori-sama|lt=Otori-sama|2=ja|3=天日鷲神|4=zh|5=天日鷲神|6=ko|7=아메노히와시노카미|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Otori-sama|qq=}} (天日鷲神)''' * '''Sugawara no Michizane (Sugawara no Michizane)''' * '''Senryū Benzaiten (筌龍弁財天)''' == History == During the reign of {{ill|Emperor Seiwa|ja|Emperor Seiwa|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Emperor Seiwa|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|WD=Q135505731}}, Fujiwara Sukemitsu was exiled due to a false accusation related to a succession dispute. In {{ill|Zhenguan|en|Zhenguan|WD=Q3577278|lt=Jōgan (era)}} 6 (864 CE), Sukemitsu was shipwrecked on the {{ill|Miura Peninsula|en|Miura Peninsula|WD=Q536757|lt=Miura Peninsula}} while traveling to his post in {{ill|Tsukushi Province|en|Tsukushi Province|WD=Q1206461|lt=Tsukushi Province}}. The locals revered Sukemitsu for his efforts in quelling pirates and improving welfare. After his death in Jōgan 8 (866 CE), a shrine was built to honor him. In {{ill|Tengen|en|Tengen|WD=Q1185206|lt=Tengen (era)}} 5 (982 CE), the current shrine building was established, and the shrine became the total guardian of {{ill|Miura District, Kanagawa|en|Miura District, Kanagawa|WD=Q1203937|lt=Miura District, Kanagawa}}. Minamoto no Yoritomo, following his 1180 uprising, held the shrine in high regard. Legend states that Yoritomo planted a pair of sacred ginkgo trees as offerings in 1185. The shrine received the title of "Sōchinju" (総鎮守, General Guardian Shrine) of the Miura Peninsula in 1719 (Kyōhō 4). It was designated a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gōsha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}} in 1873 (Meiji 6) and listed as a shrine for offering government-provided ritual offerings in 1907 (Meiji 40). The ritual {{ill|Chakkirako|en|Chakkirako|WD=Q11318123|lt=Chakkirako}}, unique to the shrine, was inscribed as a UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage in 2009. The shrine's buildings were designated as Important Cultural Properties by Kanagawa Prefecture in 2011. In 2021, the shrine became the guardian of the "Animal Shichifukujin" statues from the defunct Keikyu Aburatsubo Marine Park. == Shrine Grounds == === Main Features === * '''Main Hall (本殿)''' - Built in [[Shimmei-zukuri]] style. * '''Worship Hall (拝殿)''' - [[Ishi-no-ma-zukuri|Gongen-zukuri]] style. * '''Sacred Ginkgo Trees''' - Planted by Minamoto no Yoritomo, the female tree's drooping branches symbolize fertility and are touched by women seeking blessings for lactation and childbirth. The male tree resembles a dragon. Designated as a Natural Monument of Miura City. === Sub-Shrines === * '''Ryūjin and Suijin Shrines''' - Sacred to water and dragon deities. * '''Hōsō Shrine''' - Dedicated to Minamoto no Tametomo, protector against disease. * '''Kōya Shrine''' - Worships Iwaka Mutsukari no Mikoto, the deity of cuisine and cooking. * '''Mitama Shrine''' - Dedicated to Kamakura Goro Kagemasa, believed to heal eye diseases. * '''Fukutoku Inari Shrine''' - For prosperity and safety in trade and fishing. * '''Konpira Shrine''' - Dedicated to Ōmononushi, a deity of maritime safety and commerce. === Notable Festivals and Rituals === * '''New Year's Eve (January 1)''' - Saitan-sai with lion dances for exorcism. * '''January 15''' - {{ill|Chakkirako|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chakkirako|qq=}}: A unique dance registered as a UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage. * '''Summer Festival''' - Two-day event with traditional mikoshi processions. * '''Menkagura (November)''' - A traditional masked dance representing local folklore and Shinto traditions. == Access == * From '''Keikyu Kurihama Line''': ** Take a bus from Miura-Kaigan Station or Misaki-guchi Station to Misaki Port (三崎港), then walk 2 minutes north. * Parking available near the shrine office. == References == {{reflist}} == See Also == * {{ill|Power spot (spirituality)|en|Power spot (spirituality)|WD=Q11329568|lt=Power spots}} * [[co:commons:Category:Kainan-jinja]][[ja:海南神社]] [[co:commons:Category:Kainan-jinja]][[ja:海南神社]] [[co:commons:Category:Kainan-jinja]][[ja:海南神社]] [[sn:commons:Category:Kainan-jinja]][[ja:海南神社]] {{Infobox religious building | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | deity = deities of its local area | type = [[Sōja shrine|Sōja shrine]] religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |name = Kainan Shrine (海南神社) | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = File:Kainan-jinja ac (1).jpg |location = {{ill|Kanagawa Prefecture|en|Kanagawa Prefecture|WD=Q127513|lt=神奈川県}}, {{ill|Miura, Kanagawa|en|Miura, Kanagawa|WD=Q823886|lt=三浦市}}, [[:en:Misaki, Kanagawa|三崎]] 4丁目12-11 |position = {{coord|35|8|33.926|N|139|37|7.84|E|display=inline,title}} |enshrined_deities = * Fujiwara Sukemitsu (藤原資盈) * Mitsuwatari-hime (盈渡姫) * Senryū Benzaiten (筌龍弁財天; part of Miura Shichifukujin) * Jinushi-no-Ōkami (地主大神) |shrine_Rank = Former [[Gōsha|郷社]] |established = [[Tengen (Japan)|Tengen]] 5 (982 CE) |main_hall = [[Shimmei-zukuri|神明造]] |main_festival = Summer Festival (designated Miura City Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property)
Two days before Marine Day in July |rituals = {{ill|Chakkirako|en|Chakkirako|WD=Q11318123|lt=Chakkirako}} (UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage) |location = {{ill|Miura|WD=Q823886}} |coordinates = {{Coord|35.14275555555555|N|139.61884444444445|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} }} '''Kainan Shrine''' (海南神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} located in {{ill|Miura, Kanagawa|en|Miura, Kanagawa|WD=Q823886|lt=Miura, Kanagawa}}, {{ill|Kanagawa Prefecture|en|Kanagawa Prefecture|WD=Q127513|lt=Kanagawa Prefecture}}, slightly inland from {{ill|Misaki Fishing Port|ja|三崎漁港|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Misaki Fishing Port|1=Port of Misaki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q3316212}}. It is the total guardian shrine of the {{ill|Miura Peninsula|en|Miura Peninsula|WD=Q536757|lt=Miura Peninsula}} in {{ill|Sagami Province|en|Sagami Province|WD=Q1053732|lt=Sagami Province}}, enshrining Fujiwara Sukemitsu, Mitsuwatari-hime, Senryū Benzaiten (part of the Miura Shichifukujin), and Jinushi-no-Ōkami. The shrine has a deep connection to {{ill|Minamoto no Yoritomo|en|Minamoto no Yoritomo|WD=Q242800|lt=Minamoto no Yoritomo}}, who revered it, and it features sacred trees planted by Yoritomo, including a dragon-shaped sacred ginkgo tree. [[Kainan Shrine]] is a regional [[Sōja shrine|Sōja shrine]]. It enshrines many kami of the local region. It contrasts with provincial Soja shrines which enshrine all the kami of a provincehttps://archive.ph/wip/XtZfZ == Enshrined Deities == * '''Fujiwara Sukemitsu (藤原資盈)''' * '''Mitsuwatari-hime (盈渡姫)''' * '''Jinushi-no-Ōkami (地主大神)''' * '''Susanoo (素戔嗚尊)''' * '''{{ill|Otori-sama|ja|天日鷲神|1=Otori-sama|lt=Otori-sama|2=ja|3=天日鷲神|4=zh|5=天日鷲神|6=ko|7=아메노히와시노카미|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Otori-sama|qq=}} (天日鷲神)''' * '''Sugawara no Michizane (Sugawara no Michizane)''' * '''Senryū Benzaiten (筌龍弁財天)''' == History == During the reign of {{ill|Emperor Seiwa|ja|Emperor Seiwa|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Emperor Seiwa|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|WD=Q135505731}}, Fujiwara Sukemitsu was exiled due to a false accusation related to a succession dispute. In {{ill|Zhenguan|en|Zhenguan|WD=Q3577278|lt=Jōgan (era)}} 6 (864 CE), Sukemitsu was shipwrecked on the {{ill|Miura Peninsula|en|Miura Peninsula|WD=Q536757|lt=Miura Peninsula}} while traveling to his post in {{ill|Tsukushi Province|en|Tsukushi Province|WD=Q1206461|lt=Tsukushi Province}}. The locals revered Sukemitsu for his efforts in quelling pirates and improving welfare. After his death in Jōgan 8 (866 CE), a shrine was built to honor him. In {{ill|Tengen|en|Tengen|WD=Q1185206|lt=Tengen (era)}} 5 (982 CE), the current shrine building was established, and the shrine became the total guardian of {{ill|Miura District, Kanagawa|en|Miura District, Kanagawa|WD=Q1203937|lt=Miura District, Kanagawa}}. Minamoto no Yoritomo, following his 1180 uprising, held the shrine in high regard. Legend states that Yoritomo planted a pair of sacred ginkgo trees as offerings in 1185. The shrine received the title of "Sōchinju" (総鎮守, General Guardian Shrine) of the Miura Peninsula in 1719 (Kyōhō 4). It was designated a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gōsha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}} in 1873 (Meiji 6) and listed as a shrine for offering government-provided ritual offerings in 1907 (Meiji 40). The ritual {{ill|Chakkirako|en|Chakkirako|WD=Q11318123|lt=Chakkirako}}, unique to the shrine, was inscribed as a UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage in 2009. The shrine's buildings were designated as Important Cultural Properties by Kanagawa Prefecture in 2011. In 2021, the shrine became the guardian of the "Animal Shichifukujin" statues from the defunct Keikyu Aburatsubo Marine Park. == Shrine Grounds == === Main Features === * '''Main Hall (本殿)''' - Built in [[Shimmei-zukuri]] style. * '''Worship Hall (拝殿)''' - [[Ishi-no-ma-zukuri|Gongen-zukuri]] style. * '''Sacred Ginkgo Trees''' - Planted by Minamoto no Yoritomo, the female tree's drooping branches symbolize fertility and are touched by women seeking blessings for lactation and childbirth. The male tree resembles a dragon. Designated as a Natural Monument of Miura City. === Sub-Shrines === * '''Ryūjin and Suijin Shrines''' - Sacred to water and dragon deities. * '''Hōsō Shrine''' - Dedicated to Minamoto no Tametomo, protector against disease. * '''Kōya Shrine''' - Worships Iwaka Mutsukari no Mikoto, the deity of cuisine and cooking. * '''Mitama Shrine''' - Dedicated to Kamakura Goro Kagemasa, believed to heal eye diseases. * '''Fukutoku Inari Shrine''' - For prosperity and safety in trade and fishing. * '''Konpira Shrine''' - Dedicated to Ōmononushi, a deity of maritime safety and commerce. === Notable Festivals and Rituals === * '''New Year's Eve (January 1)''' - Saitan-sai with lion dances for exorcism. * '''January 15''' - {{ill|Chakkirako|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chakkirako|qq=}}: A unique dance registered as a UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage. * '''Summer Festival''' - Two-day event with traditional mikoshi processions. * '''Menkagura (November)''' - A traditional masked dance representing local folklore and Shinto traditions. == Access == * From '''Keikyu Kurihama Line''': ** Take a bus from Miura-Kaigan Station or Misaki-guchi Station to Misaki Port (三崎港), then walk 2 minutes north. * Parking available near the shrine office. == References == {{reflist}} == See Also == * {{ill|Power spot (spirituality)|en|Power spot (spirituality)|WD=Q11329568|lt=Power spots}} * [[co:commons:Category:Kainan-jinja]][[ja:海南神社]] [[co:commons:Category:Kainan-jinja]][[ja:海南神社]] [[co:commons:Category:Kainan-jinja]][[ja:海南神社]] [[sn:commons:Category:Kainan-jinja]][[ja:海南神社]] {{Infobox religious building | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | deity = deities of its local area | type = [[Sōja shrine|Sōja shrine]] religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |name = Kainan Shrine (海南神社) | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = File:Kainan-jinja ac (1).jpg |location = {{ill|Kanagawa Prefecture|en|Kanagawa Prefecture|WD=Q127513|lt=神奈川県|1=Kanagawa Prefecture}}, {{ill|Miura, Kanagawa|en|Miura, Kanagawa|WD=Q823886|lt=三浦市|1=Miura, Kanagawa}}, [[:en:Misaki, Kanagawa|三崎]] 4丁目12-11 |position = {{coord|35|8|33.926|N|139|37|7.84|E|display=inline,title}} |enshrined_deities = * Fujiwara Sukemitsu (藤原資盈) * Mitsuwatari-hime (盈渡姫) * Senryū Benzaiten (筌龍弁財天; part of Miura Shichifukujin) * Jinushi-no-Ōkami (地主大神) |shrine_Rank = Former [[Gōsha|郷社]] |established = [[Tengen (Japan)|Tengen]] 5 (982 CE) |main_hall = [[Shimmei-zukuri|神明造]] |main_festival = Summer Festival (designated Miura City Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property)
Two days before Marine Day in July |rituals = {{ill|Chakkirako|en|Chakkirako|WD=Q11318123|lt=Chakkirako|1=Chakkirako}} (UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage) |location = {{ill|Miura|WD=Q823886|1=Miura, Kanagawa}} |coordinates = {{Coord|35.14275555555555|N|139.61884444444445|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} }} '''Kainan Shrine''' (海南神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine|1=Shinto shrine}} located in {{ill|Miura, Kanagawa|en|Miura, Kanagawa|WD=Q823886|lt=Miura, Kanagawa|1=Miura, Kanagawa}}, {{ill|Kanagawa Prefecture|en|Kanagawa Prefecture|WD=Q127513|lt=Kanagawa Prefecture|1=Kanagawa Prefecture}}, slightly inland from {{ill|Misaki Fishing Port|ja|三崎漁港|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Misaki Fishing Port|1=Port of Misaki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q3316212}}. It is the total guardian shrine of the {{ill|Miura Peninsula|en|Miura Peninsula|WD=Q536757|lt=Miura Peninsula|1=Miura Peninsula}} in {{ill|Sagami Province|en|Sagami Province|WD=Q1053732|lt=Sagami Province|1=Sagami Province}}, enshrining Fujiwara Sukemitsu, Mitsuwatari-hime, Senryū Benzaiten (part of the Miura Shichifukujin), and Jinushi-no-Ōkami. The shrine has a deep connection to {{ill|Minamoto no Yoritomo|en|Minamoto no Yoritomo|WD=Q242800|lt=Minamoto no Yoritomo|1=Minamoto no Yoritomo}}, who revered it, and it features sacred trees planted by Yoritomo, including a dragon-shaped sacred ginkgo tree. [[Kainan Shrine]] is a regional [[Sōja shrine|Sōja shrine]]. It enshrines many kami of the local region. It contrasts with provincial Soja shrines which enshrine all the kami of a provincehttps://archive.ph/wip/XtZfZ == Enshrined Deities == * '''Fujiwara Sukemitsu (藤原資盈)''' * '''Mitsuwatari-hime (盈渡姫)''' * '''Jinushi-no-Ōkami (地主大神)''' * '''Susanoo (素戔嗚尊)''' * '''{{ill|Otori-sama|ja|天日鷲神|1=Otori-sama|lt=Otori-sama|2=ja|3=天日鷲神|4=zh|5=天日鷲神|6=ko|7=아메노히와시노카미|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Otori-sama|qq=}} (天日鷲神)''' * '''Sugawara no Michizane (Sugawara no Michizane)''' * '''Senryū Benzaiten (筌龍弁財天)''' == History == During the reign of {{ill|Emperor Seiwa|ja|Emperor Seiwa|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Emperor Seiwa|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|WD=Q135505731|1=Emperor Seiwa}}, Fujiwara Sukemitsu was exiled due to a false accusation related to a succession dispute. In {{ill|Zhenguan|en|Zhenguan|WD=Q3577278|lt=Jōgan (era)|1=Zhenguan}} 6 (864 CE), Sukemitsu was shipwrecked on the {{ill|Miura Peninsula|en|Miura Peninsula|WD=Q536757|lt=Miura Peninsula|1=Miura Peninsula}} while traveling to his post in {{ill|Tsukushi Province|en|Tsukushi Province|WD=Q1206461|lt=Tsukushi Province|1=Tsukushi Province}}. The locals revered Sukemitsu for his efforts in quelling pirates and improving welfare. After his death in Jōgan 8 (866 CE), a shrine was built to honor him. In {{ill|Tengen|en|Tengen|WD=Q1185206|lt=Tengen (era)|1=Tengen}} 5 (982 CE), the current shrine building was established, and the shrine became the total guardian of {{ill|Miura District, Kanagawa|en|Miura District, Kanagawa|WD=Q1203937|lt=Miura District, Kanagawa|1=Miura District, Kanagawa}}. Minamoto no Yoritomo, following his 1180 uprising, held the shrine in high regard. Legend states that Yoritomo planted a pair of sacred ginkgo trees as offerings in 1185. The shrine received the title of "Sōchinju" (総鎮守, General Guardian Shrine) of the Miura Peninsula in 1719 (Kyōhō 4). It was designated a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|WD=Q90139226|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gōsha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}} in 1873 (Meiji 6) and listed as a shrine for offering government-provided ritual offerings in 1907 (Meiji 40). The ritual {{ill|Chakkirako|en|Chakkirako|WD=Q11318123|lt=Chakkirako|1=Chakkirako}}, unique to the shrine, was inscribed as a UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage in 2009. The shrine's buildings were designated as Important Cultural Properties by Kanagawa Prefecture in 2011. In 2021, the shrine became the guardian of the "Animal Shichifukujin" statues from the defunct Keikyu Aburatsubo Marine Park. == Shrine Grounds == === Main Features === * '''Main Hall (本殿)''' - Built in [[Shimmei-zukuri]] style. * '''Worship Hall (拝殿)''' - [[Ishi-no-ma-zukuri|Gongen-zukuri]] style. * '''Sacred Ginkgo Trees''' - Planted by Minamoto no Yoritomo, the female tree's drooping branches symbolize fertility and are touched by women seeking blessings for lactation and childbirth. The male tree resembles a dragon. Designated as a Natural Monument of Miura City. === Sub-Shrines === * '''Ryūjin and Suijin Shrines''' - Sacred to water and dragon deities. * '''Hōsō Shrine''' - Dedicated to Minamoto no Tametomo, protector against disease. * '''Kōya Shrine''' - Worships Iwaka Mutsukari no Mikoto, the deity of cuisine and cooking. * '''Mitama Shrine''' - Dedicated to Kamakura Goro Kagemasa, believed to heal eye diseases. * '''Fukutoku Inari Shrine''' - For prosperity and safety in trade and fishing. * '''Konpira Shrine''' - Dedicated to Ōmononushi, a deity of maritime safety and commerce. === Notable Festivals and Rituals === * '''New Year's Eve (January 1)''' - Saitan-sai with lion dances for exorcism. * '''January 15''' - {{ill|Chakkirako|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chakkirako|qq=}}: A unique dance registered as a UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage. * '''Summer Festival''' - Two-day event with traditional mikoshi processions. * '''Menkagura (November)''' - A traditional masked dance representing local folklore and Shinto traditions. == Access == * From '''Keikyu Kurihama Line''': ** Take a bus from Miura-Kaigan Station or Misaki-guchi Station to Misaki Port (三崎港), then walk 2 minutes north. * Parking available near the shrine office. == References == {{reflist}} == See Also == * {{ill|Power spot (spirituality)|en|Power spot (spirituality)|WD=Q11329568|lt=Power spots|1=Power spot (spirituality)}} * {{ill|Minamoto no Yoritomo|en|Minamoto no Yoritomo|WD=Q242800|lt=Minamoto no Yoritomo|1=Minamoto no Yoritomo}} * Two days before Marine Day in July |rituals = {{ill|Chakkirako|en|Chakkirako|WD=Q11318123|lt=Chakkirako|1=Chakkirako}} (UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage) |location = {{ill|Miura|WD=Q823886|1=Miura, Kanagawa}} |coordinates = {{Coord|35.14275555555555|N|139.61884444444445|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} }} '''Kainan Shrine''' (海南神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine|1=Shinto shrine}} located in {{ill|Miura, Kanagawa|en|Miura, Kanagawa|WD=Q823886|lt=Miura, Kanagawa|1=Miura, Kanagawa}}, {{ill|Kanagawa Prefecture|en|Kanagawa Prefecture|WD=Q127513|lt=Kanagawa Prefecture|1=Kanagawa Prefecture}}, slightly inland from {{ill|Misaki Fishing Port|ja|三崎漁港|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Misaki Fishing Port|1=Port of Misaki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q3316212}}. It is the total guardian shrine of the {{ill|Miura Peninsula|en|Miura Peninsula|WD=Q536757|lt=Miura Peninsula|1=Miura Peninsula}} in {{ill|Sagami Province|en|Sagami Province|WD=Q1053732|lt=Sagami Province|1=Sagami Province}}, enshrining Fujiwara Sukemitsu, Mitsuwatari-hime, Senryū Benzaiten (part of the Miura Shichifukujin), and Jinushi-no-Ōkami. The shrine has a deep connection to {{ill|Minamoto no Yoritomo|en|Minamoto no Yoritomo|WD=Q242800|lt=Minamoto no Yoritomo|1=Minamoto no Yoritomo}}, who revered it, and it features sacred trees planted by Yoritomo, including a dragon-shaped sacred ginkgo tree. [[Kainan Shrine]] is a regional [[Sōja shrine|Sōja shrine]]. It enshrines many kami of the local region. It contrasts with provincial Soja shrines which enshrine all the kami of a provincehttps://archive.ph/wip/XtZfZ == Enshrined Deities == * '''Fujiwara Sukemitsu (藤原資盈)''' * '''Mitsuwatari-hime (盈渡姫)''' * '''Jinushi-no-Ōkami (地主大神)''' * '''Susanoo (素戔嗚尊)''' * '''{{ill|Otori-sama|ja|天日鷲神|1=Otori-sama|lt=Otori-sama|2=ja|3=天日鷲神|4=zh|5=天日鷲神|6=ko|7=아메노히와시노카미|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Otori-sama|qq=}} (天日鷲神)''' * '''Sugawara no Michizane (Sugawara no Michizane)''' * '''Senryū Benzaiten (筌龍弁財天)''' == History == During the reign of {{ill|Emperor Seiwa|ja|Emperor Seiwa|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Emperor Seiwa|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|WD=Q135505731|1=Emperor Seiwa}}, Fujiwara Sukemitsu was exiled due to a false accusation related to a succession dispute. In {{ill|Zhenguan|en|Zhenguan|WD=Q3577278|lt=Jōgan (era)|1=Zhenguan}} 6 (864 CE), Sukemitsu was shipwrecked on the {{ill|Miura Peninsula|en|Miura Peninsula|WD=Q536757|lt=Miura Peninsula|1=Miura Peninsula}} while traveling to his post in {{ill|Tsukushi Province|en|Tsukushi Province|WD=Q1206461|lt=Tsukushi Province|1=Tsukushi Province}}. The locals revered Sukemitsu for his efforts in quelling pirates and improving welfare. After his death in Jōgan 8 (866 CE), a shrine was built to honor him. In {{ill|Tengen|en|Tengen|WD=Q1185206|lt=Tengen (era)|1=Tengen}} 5 (982 CE), the current shrine building was established, and the shrine became the total guardian of {{ill|Miura District, Kanagawa|en|Miura District, Kanagawa|WD=Q1203937|lt=Miura District, Kanagawa|1=Miura District, Kanagawa}}. Minamoto no Yoritomo, following his 1180 uprising, held the shrine in high regard. Legend states that Yoritomo planted a pair of sacred ginkgo trees as offerings in 1185. The shrine received the title of "Sōchinju" (総鎮守, General Guardian Shrine) of the Miura Peninsula in 1719 (Kyōhō 4). It was designated a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|WD=Q90139226|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gōsha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}} in 1873 (Meiji 6) and listed as a shrine for offering government-provided ritual offerings in 1907 (Meiji 40). The ritual {{ill|Chakkirako|en|Chakkirako|WD=Q11318123|lt=Chakkirako|1=Chakkirako}}, unique to the shrine, was inscribed as a UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage in 2009. The shrine's buildings were designated as Important Cultural Properties by Kanagawa Prefecture in 2011. In 2021, the shrine became the guardian of the "Animal Shichifukujin" statues from the defunct Keikyu Aburatsubo Marine Park. == Shrine Grounds == === Main Features === * '''Main Hall (本殿)''' - Built in [[Shimmei-zukuri]] style. * '''Worship Hall (拝殿)''' - [[Ishi-no-ma-zukuri|Gongen-zukuri]] style. * '''Sacred Ginkgo Trees''' - Planted by Minamoto no Yoritomo, the female tree's drooping branches symbolize fertility and are touched by women seeking blessings for lactation and childbirth. The male tree resembles a dragon. Designated as a Natural Monument of Miura City. === Sub-Shrines === * '''Ryūjin and Suijin Shrines''' - Sacred to water and dragon deities. * '''Hōsō Shrine''' - Dedicated to Minamoto no Tametomo, protector against disease. * '''Kōya Shrine''' - Worships Iwaka Mutsukari no Mikoto, the deity of cuisine and cooking. * '''Mitama Shrine''' - Dedicated to Kamakura Goro Kagemasa, believed to heal eye diseases. * '''Fukutoku Inari Shrine''' - For prosperity and safety in trade and fishing. * '''Konpira Shrine''' - Dedicated to Ōmononushi, a deity of maritime safety and commerce. === Notable Festivals and Rituals === * '''New Year's Eve (January 1)''' - Saitan-sai with lion dances for exorcism. * '''January 15''' - {{ill|Chakkirako|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chakkirako|qq=}}: A unique dance registered as a UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage. * '''Summer Festival''' - Two-day event with traditional mikoshi processions. * '''Menkagura (November)''' - A traditional masked dance representing local folklore and Shinto traditions. == Access == * From '''Keikyu Kurihama Line''': ** Take a bus from Miura-Kaigan Station or Misaki-guchi Station to Misaki Port (三崎港), then walk 2 minutes north. * Parking available near the shrine office. == References == {{reflist}} == See Also == * {{ill|Power spot (spirituality)|en|Power spot (spirituality)|WD=Q11329568|lt=Power [[co:commons:Category:Kainan-jinja]][[ja:海南神社]] [[co:commons:Category:Kainan-jinja]][[ja:海南神社]] [[co:commons:Category:Kainan-jinja]][[ja:海南神社]] [[Category:sn_crud|TESTcommons:Category:Kainan-jinja]][[ja:海南神社]] {{Infobox religious building | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | deity = deities of its local area | type = [[Sōja shrine|Sōja shrine]] religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |name = Kainan Shrine (海南神社) | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] |image = File:Kainan-jinja ac (1).jpg |location = {{ill|Kanagawa Prefecture|en|Kanagawa Prefecture|WD=Q127513|lt=神奈川県|1=Kanagawa Prefecture}}, {{ill|Miura, Kanagawa|en|Miura, Kanagawa|WD=Q823886|lt=三浦市|1=Miura, Kanagawa}}, [[:en:Misaki, Kanagawa|三崎]] 4丁目12-11 |position = {{coord|35|8|33.926|N|139|37|7.84|E|display=inline,title}} |enshrined_deities = * Fujiwara Sukemitsu (藤原資盈) * Mitsuwatari-hime (盈渡姫) * Senryū Benzaiten (筌龍弁財天; part of Miura Shichifukujin) * Jinushi-no-Ōkami (地主大神) |shrine_Rank = Former [[Gōsha|郷社]] |established = [[Tengen (Japan)|Tengen]] 5 (982 CE) |main_hall = [[Shimmei-zukuri|神明造]] |main_festival = Summer Festival (designated Miura City Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property)
Two days before Marine Day in July |rituals = {{ill|Chakkirako|en|Chakkirako|WD=Q11318123|lt=Chakkirako|1=Chakkirako}} (UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage) |location = {{ill|Miura|WD=Q823886|1=Miura, Kanagawa}} |coordinates = {{Coord|35.14275555555555|N|139.61884444444445|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} }} '''Kainan Shrine''' (海南神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine|1=Shinto shrine}} located in {{ill|Miura, Kanagawa|en|Miura, Kanagawa|WD=Q823886|lt=Miura, Kanagawa|1=Miura, Kanagawa}}, {{ill|Kanagawa Prefecture|en|Kanagawa Prefecture|WD=Q127513|lt=Kanagawa Prefecture|1=Kanagawa Prefecture}}, slightly inland from {{ill|Misaki Fishing Port|ja|三崎漁港|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Misaki Fishing Port|1=Port of Misaki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q3316212}}. It is the total guardian shrine of the {{ill|Miura Peninsula|en|Miura Peninsula|WD=Q536757|lt=Miura Peninsula|1=Miura Peninsula}} in {{ill|Sagami Province|en|Sagami Province|WD=Q1053732|lt=Sagami Province|1=Sagami Province}}, enshrining Fujiwara Sukemitsu, Mitsuwatari-hime, Senryū Benzaiten (part of the Miura Shichifukujin), and Jinushi-no-Ōkami. The shrine has a deep connection to {{ill|Minamoto no Yoritomo|en|Minamoto no Yoritomo|WD=Q242800|lt=Minamoto no Yoritomo|1=Minamoto no Yoritomo}}, who revered it, and it features sacred trees planted by Yoritomo, including a dragon-shaped sacred ginkgo tree. [[Kainan Shrine]] is a regional [[Sōja shrine|Sōja shrine]]. It enshrines many kami of the local region. It contrasts with provincial Soja shrines which enshrine all the kami of a provincehttps://archive.ph/wip/XtZfZ == Enshrined Deities == * '''Fujiwara Sukemitsu (藤原資盈)''' * '''Mitsuwatari-hime (盈渡姫)''' * '''Jinushi-no-Ōkami (地主大神)''' * '''Susanoo (素戔嗚尊)''' * '''{{ill|Otori-sama|ja|天日鷲神|1=Otori-sama|lt=Otori-sama|2=ja|3=天日鷲神|4=zh|5=天日鷲神|6=ko|7=아메노히와시노카미|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Otori-sama|qq=}} (天日鷲神)''' * '''Sugawara no Michizane (Sugawara no Michizane)''' * '''Senryū Benzaiten (筌龍弁財天)''' == History == During the reign of {{ill|Emperor Seiwa|ja|Emperor Seiwa|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Emperor Seiwa|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|WD=Q135505731|1=Emperor Seiwa}}, Fujiwara Sukemitsu was exiled due to a false accusation related to a succession dispute. In {{ill|Zhenguan|en|Zhenguan|WD=Q3577278|lt=Jōgan (era)|1=Zhenguan}} 6 (864 CE), Sukemitsu was shipwrecked on the {{ill|Miura Peninsula|en|Miura Peninsula|WD=Q536757|lt=Miura Peninsula|1=Miura Peninsula}} while traveling to his post in {{ill|Tsukushi Province|en|Tsukushi Province|WD=Q1206461|lt=Tsukushi Province|1=Tsukushi Province}}. The locals revered Sukemitsu for his efforts in quelling pirates and improving welfare. After his death in Jōgan 8 (866 CE), a shrine was built to honor him. In {{ill|Tengen|en|Tengen|WD=Q1185206|lt=Tengen (era)|1=Tengen}} 5 (982 CE), the current shrine building was established, and the shrine became the total guardian of {{ill|Miura District, Kanagawa|en|Miura District, Kanagawa|WD=Q1203937|lt=Miura District, Kanagawa|1=Miura District, Kanagawa}}. Minamoto no Yoritomo, following his 1180 uprising, held the shrine in high regard. Legend states that Yoritomo planted a pair of sacred ginkgo trees as offerings in 1185. The shrine received the title of "Sōchinju" (総鎮守, General Guardian Shrine) of the Miura Peninsula in 1719 (Kyōhō 4). It was designated a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|WD=Q90139226|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gōsha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}} in 1873 (Meiji 6) and listed as a shrine for offering government-provided ritual offerings in 1907 (Meiji 40). The ritual {{ill|Chakkirako|en|Chakkirako|WD=Q11318123|lt=Chakkirako|1=Chakkirako}}, unique to the shrine, was inscribed as a UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage in 2009. The shrine's buildings were designated as Important Cultural Properties by Kanagawa Prefecture in 2011. In 2021, the shrine became the guardian of the "Animal Shichifukujin" statues from the defunct Keikyu Aburatsubo Marine Park. == Shrine Grounds == === Main Features === * '''Main Hall (本殿)''' - Built in [[Shimmei-zukuri]] style. * '''Worship Hall (拝殿)''' - [[Ishi-no-ma-zukuri|Gongen-zukuri]] style. * '''Sacred Ginkgo Trees''' - Planted by Minamoto no Yoritomo, the female tree's drooping branches symbolize fertility and are touched by women seeking blessings for lactation and childbirth. The male tree resembles a dragon. Designated as a Natural Monument of Miura City. === Sub-Shrines === * '''Ryūjin and Suijin Shrines''' - Sacred to water and dragon deities. * '''Hōsō Shrine''' - Dedicated to Minamoto no Tametomo, protector against disease. * '''Kōya Shrine''' - Worships Iwaka Mutsukari no Mikoto, the deity of cuisine and cooking. * '''Mitama Shrine''' - Dedicated to Kamakura Goro Kagemasa, believed to heal eye diseases. * '''Fukutoku Inari Shrine''' - For prosperity and safety in trade and fishing. * '''Konpira Shrine''' - Dedicated to Ōmononushi, a deity of maritime safety and commerce. === Notable Festivals and Rituals === * '''New Year's Eve (January 1)''' - Saitan-sai with lion dances for exorcism. * '''January 15''' - {{ill|Chakkirako|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chakkirako|qq=}}: A unique dance registered as a UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage. * '''Summer Festival''' - Two-day event with traditional mikoshi processions. * '''Menkagura (November)''' - A traditional masked dance representing local folklore and Shinto traditions. == Access == * From '''Keikyu Kurihama Line''': ** Take a bus from Miura-Kaigan Station or Misaki-guchi Station to Misaki Port (三崎港), then walk 2 minutes north. * Parking available near the shrine office. == References == {{reflist}} == See Also == * {{ill|Power spot (spirituality)|en|Power spot (spirituality)|WD=Q11329568|lt=Power spots|1=Power spot (spirituality)}} * {{ill|Minamoto no Yoritomo|en|Minamoto no Yoritomo|WD=Q242800|lt=Minamoto no Yoritomo|1=Minamoto no Yoritomo}} * Two days before Marine Day in July |rituals = {{ill|Chakkirako|en|Chakkirako|WD=Q11318123|lt=Chakkirako|1=Chakkirako}} (UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage) |location = {{ill|Miura|WD=Q823886|1=Miura, Kanagawa}} |coordinates = {{Coord|35.14275555555555|N|139.61884444444445|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} }} '''Kainan Shrine''' (海南神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine|1=Shinto shrine}} located in {{ill|Miura, Kanagawa|en|Miura, Kanagawa|WD=Q823886|lt=Miura, Kanagawa|1=Miura, Kanagawa}}, {{ill|Kanagawa Prefecture|en|Kanagawa Prefecture|WD=Q127513|lt=Kanagawa Prefecture|1=Kanagawa Prefecture}}, slightly inland from {{ill|Misaki Fishing Port|ja|三崎漁港|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Misaki Fishing Port|1=Port of Misaki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q3316212}}. It is the total guardian shrine of the {{ill|Miura Peninsula|en|Miura Peninsula|WD=Q536757|lt=Miura Peninsula|1=Miura Peninsula}} in {{ill|Sagami Province|en|Sagami Province|WD=Q1053732|lt=Sagami Province|1=Sagami Province}}, enshrining Fujiwara Sukemitsu, Mitsuwatari-hime, Senryū Benzaiten (part of the Miura Shichifukujin), and Jinushi-no-Ōkami. The shrine has a deep connection to {{ill|Minamoto no Yoritomo|en|Minamoto no Yoritomo|WD=Q242800|lt=Minamoto no Yoritomo|1=Minamoto no Yoritomo}}, who revered it, and it features sacred trees planted by Yoritomo, including a dragon-shaped sacred ginkgo tree. [[Kainan Shrine]] is a regional [[Sōja shrine|Sōja shrine]]. It enshrines many kami of the local region. It contrasts with provincial Soja shrines which enshrine all the kami of a provincehttps://archive.ph/wip/XtZfZ == Enshrined Deities == * '''Fujiwara Sukemitsu (藤原資盈)''' * '''Mitsuwatari-hime (盈渡姫)''' * '''Jinushi-no-Ōkami (地主大神)''' * '''Susanoo (素戔嗚尊)''' * '''{{ill|Otori-sama|ja|天日鷲神|1=Otori-sama|lt=Otori-sama|2=ja|3=天日鷲神|4=zh|5=天日鷲神|6=ko|7=아메노히와시노카미|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Otori-sama|qq=}} (天日鷲神)''' * '''Sugawara no Michizane (Sugawara no Michizane)''' * '''Senryū Benzaiten (筌龍弁財天)''' == History == During the reign of {{ill|Emperor Seiwa|ja|Emperor Seiwa|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Emperor Seiwa|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|WD=Q135505731|1=Emperor Seiwa}}, Fujiwara Sukemitsu was exiled due to a false accusation related to a succession dispute. In {{ill|Zhenguan|en|Zhenguan|WD=Q3577278|lt=Jōgan (era)|1=Zhenguan}} 6 (864 CE), Sukemitsu was shipwrecked on the {{ill|Miura Peninsula|en|Miura Peninsula|WD=Q536757|lt=Miura Peninsula|1=Miura Peninsula}} while traveling to his post in {{ill|Tsukushi Province|en|Tsukushi Province|WD=Q1206461|lt=Tsukushi Province|1=Tsukushi Province}}. The locals revered Sukemitsu for his efforts in quelling pirates and improving welfare. After his death in Jōgan 8 (866 CE), a shrine was built to honor him. In {{ill|Tengen|en|Tengen|WD=Q1185206|lt=Tengen (era)|1=Tengen}} 5 (982 CE), the current shrine building was established, and the shrine became the total guardian of {{ill|Miura District, Kanagawa|en|Miura District, Kanagawa|WD=Q1203937|lt=Miura District, Kanagawa|1=Miura District, Kanagawa}}. Minamoto no Yoritomo, following his 1180 uprising, held the shrine in high regard. Legend states that Yoritomo planted a pair of sacred ginkgo trees as offerings in 1185. The shrine received the title of "Sōchinju" (総鎮守, General Guardian Shrine) of the Miura Peninsula in 1719 (Kyōhō 4). It was designated a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社|1=Gō-sha|WD=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|WD=Q90139226|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gōsha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}} in 1873 (Meiji 6) and listed as a shrine for offering government-provided ritual offerings in 1907 (Meiji 40). The ritual {{ill|Chakkirako|en|Chakkirako|WD=Q11318123|lt=Chakkirako|1=Chakkirako}}, unique to the shrine, was inscribed as a UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage in 2009. The shrine's buildings were designated as Important Cultural Properties by Kanagawa Prefecture in 2011. In 2021, the shrine became the guardian of the "Animal Shichifukujin" statues from the defunct Keikyu Aburatsubo Marine Park. == Shrine Grounds == === Main Features === * '''Main Hall (本殿)''' - Built in [[Shimmei-zukuri]] style. * '''Worship Hall (拝殿)''' - [[Ishi-no-ma-zukuri|Gongen-zukuri]] style. * '''Sacred Ginkgo Trees''' - Planted by Minamoto no Yoritomo, the female tree's drooping branches symbolize fertility and are touched by women seeking blessings for lactation and childbirth. The male tree resembles a dragon. Designated as a Natural Monument of Miura City. === Sub-Shrines === * '''Ryūjin and Suijin Shrines''' - Sacred to water and dragon deities. * '''Hōsō Shrine''' - Dedicated to Minamoto no Tametomo, protector against disease. * '''Kōya Shrine''' - Worships Iwaka Mutsukari no Mikoto, the deity of cuisine and cooking. * '''Mitama Shrine''' - Dedicated to Kamakura Goro Kagemasa, believed to heal eye diseases. * '''Fukutoku Inari Shrine''' - For prosperity and safety in trade and fishing. * '''Konpira Shrine''' - Dedicated to Ōmononushi, a deity of maritime safety and commerce. === Notable Festivals and Rituals === * '''New Year's Eve (January 1)''' - Saitan-sai with lion dances for exorcism. * '''January 15''' - {{ill|Chakkirako|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chakkirako|qq=}}: A unique dance registered as a UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage. * '''Summer Festival''' - Two-day event with traditional mikoshi processions. * '''Menkagura (November)''' - A traditional masked dance representing local folklore and Shinto traditions. == Access == * From '''Keikyu Kurihama Line''': ** Take a bus from Miura-Kaigan Station or Misaki-guchi Station to Misaki Port (三崎港), then walk 2 Two days before Marine Day in July |rituals = {{ill|Chakkirako|en|Chakkirako|qid=Q11318123|lt=Chakkirako|1=Chakkirako}} (UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage) |location = {{ill|Miura|qid=Q823886|1=Miura, Kanagawa}} |coordinates = {{Coord|35.14275555555555|N|139.61884444444445|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} }} '''Kainan Shrine''' (海南神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|qid=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine|1=Shinto shrine}} located in {{ill|Miura, Kanagawa|en|Miura, Kanagawa|qid=Q823886|lt=Miura, Kanagawa|1=Miura, Kanagawa}}, {{ill|Kanagawa Prefecture|en|Kanagawa Prefecture|qid=Q127513|lt=Kanagawa Prefecture|1=Kanagawa Prefecture}}, slightly inland from {{ill|Misaki Fishing Port|ja|三崎漁港|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Misaki Fishing Port|1=Port of Misaki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q3316212}}. It is the total guardian shrine of the {{ill|Miura Peninsula|en|Miura Peninsula|qid=Q536757|lt=Miura Peninsula|1=Miura Peninsula}} in {{ill|Sagami Province|en|Sagami Province|qid=Q1053732|lt=Sagami Province|1=Sagami Province}}, enshrining Fujiwara Sukemitsu, Mitsuwatari-hime, Senryū Benzaiten (part of the Miura Shichifukujin), and Jinushi-no-Ōkami. The shrine has a deep connection to {{ill|Minamoto no Yoritomo|en|Minamoto no Yoritomo|qid=Q242800|lt=Minamoto no Yoritomo|1=Minamoto no Yoritomo}}, who revered it, and it features sacred trees planted by Yoritomo, including a dragon-shaped sacred ginkgo tree. [[Kainan Shrine]] is a regional [[Sōja shrine|Sōja shrine]]. It enshrines many kami of the local region. It contrasts with provincial Soja shrines which enshrine all the kami of a provincehttps://archive.ph/wip/XtZfZ == Enshrined Deities == * '''Fujiwara Sukemitsu (藤原資盈)''' * '''Mitsuwatari-hime (盈渡姫)''' * '''Jinushi-no-Ōkami (地主大神)''' * '''Susanoo (素戔嗚尊)''' * '''{{ill|Otori-sama|ja|天日鷲神|1=Otori-sama|lt=Otori-sama|2=ja|3=天日鷲神|4=zh|5=天日鷲神|6=ko|7=아메노히와시노카미|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Otori-sama|qq=}} (天日鷲神)''' * '''Sugawara no Michizane (Sugawara no Michizane)''' * '''Senryū Benzaiten (筌龍弁財天)''' == History == During the reign of {{ill|Emperor Seiwa|ja|Emperor Seiwa|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Emperor Seiwa|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|qid=Q135505731|1=Emperor Seiwa}}, Fujiwara Sukemitsu was exiled due to a false accusation related to a succession dispute.
